(timestamped on the platform's servers); the transcript is what the assessors
actually read. They will be cross-checked.

Chat, or Claude Code in agent mode), write *"not available"* under share links

### What counts as editing

* **Allowed:** removing personal identifiers (real names, emails, API keys);
redacting any unrelated personal chats accidentally captured in the export;
fixing copy-paste artefacts (stray HTML tags) into clean text.
* **Not allowed:** deleting messages, summarising responses, rewriting your
messages afterwards, reordering turns, removing exchanges that look
embarrassing or off-track.

If you make redactions, note them briefly at the top of the relevant session
(e.g., *"Redacted: two unrelated personal messages between turn 4 and turn 5."*).
That transparency is itself a positive signal.

8/26/2026, 8:52:56 PM



Yes — the standard pandas .corr() is primarily for numeric data.



For example:



df.corr()



will calculate correlations between numeric columns. Categorical/text columns such as:



parcel\_category

comments

booking\_status

room\_type



cannot directly be used in a standard Pearson correlation matrix.



But categorical variables can still be analyzed



You have a few options depending on the type of categorical variable:



Variable type

Suitable approach

Numeric ↔ Numeric

Pearson/Spearman correlation

Binary ↔ Numeric

Point-biserial correlation

Categorical ↔ Categorical

Cramér's V / Chi-square

Categorical ↔ Numeric

ANOVA / correlation ratio (η)

Text (comments)

NLP/text features first



For your ML dataset, a common approach is to encode categorical variables first. For example:



df\_encoded = pd.get\_dummies(df, columns=\["parcel\_category"])



Then the resulting 0/1 columns can be included in a correlation analysis.



However, don't blindly label-encode categories like:



bb = 0

hb = 1

fb = 2



and then interpret Pearson correlation. The numbers are arbitrary, so the resulting correlation can be misleading.



For your current heatmap, your approach of:



corr\_cols = \[

&#x20;   col for col in merged.columns

&#x20;   if col not in excluded\_columns

&#x20;   and pd.api.types.is\_numeric\_dtype(merged\[col])

]



is the correct/simple approach if you specifically want a numeric correlation matrix.

The important point is that .corr() only works directly with numeric columns. So if corr\_cols contains columns such as hotel, arrival\_date\_month, meal, country, etc., you need to select numeric columns first.



Recommended code



\# Target column

target = "is\_canceled"



\# Exclude columns that should not be considered

excluded\_columns = {"comments", "booking\_id", "Unnamed: 0"}



\# Select numeric columns only, excluding target from the feature list

&#x20;   col for col in merged.columns

&#x20;   if col not in excluded\_columns

&#x20;   and pd.api.types.is\_numeric\_dtype(merged\[col])

]



\# Calculate correlation against is\_canceled

corr\_with\_target = (

&#x20;   merged\[corr\_cols + \[target]]

&#x20;   .corr()\[\[target]]

&#x20;   .drop(target)

&#x20;   .sort\_values(by=target, ascending=False)

)

Yes. If you want is\_canceled on the Y-axis and each other column on the X-axis to see how it relates to cancellation, you should not use .corr() for all these columns, because many of them are categorical.



For your current list, a good approach is:



Numeric columns → plot average is\_canceled



Categorical columns → plot cancellation rate by category



is\_canceled itself → exclude it as a feature



You can also automatically generate the plots 8 per figure.



import math

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import seaborn as sns

import pandas as pd



sns.set\_theme(style="whitegrid")



target = "is\_canceled"



cols = \[

&#x20;   "hotel", "lead\_time", "arrival\_date\_year",

&#x20;   "arrival\_date\_month", "stays\_in\_weekend\_nights",

&#x20;   "stays\_in\_week\_nights", "adults", "children", "babies",

&#x20;   "meal", "country", "market\_segment", "distribution\_channel",

&#x20;   "is\_repeated\_guest", "booking\_changes", "deposit\_type",

&#x20;   "agent", "company", "days\_in\_waiting\_list", "customer\_type",

&#x20;   "required\_car\_parking\_spaces", "total\_of\_special\_requests"

]



plots\_per\_figure = 8



for start in range(0, len(cols), plots\_per\_figure):



&#x20;   plot\_cols = cols\[start:start + plots\_per\_figure]



&#x20;   fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(18, 10))

&#x20;   axes = axes.ravel()



&#x20;   for ax, col in zip(axes, plot\_cols):



&#x20;       # Calculate cancellation rate for each value

&#x20;       cancellation\_rate = (

&#x20;           df.groupby(col, dropna=False)\[target]

&#x20;           .mean()

&#x20;           .sort\_values(ascending=False)

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       cancellation\_rate.plot(

&#x20;           kind="bar",

&#x20;           ax=ax

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       ax.set\_title(f"{col} vs {target}")

&#x20;       ax.set\_xlabel(col)

&#x20;       ax.set\_ylabel("Cancellation Rate")

&#x20;       ax.tick\_params(axis="x", rotation=45)



&#x20;   # Hide unused plots

&#x20;   for ax in axes\[len(plot\_cols):]:

&#x20;       ax.set\_visible(False)



&#x20;   plt.tight\_layout()

&#x20;   plt.show()



What the Y-axis represents



For example, for deposit\_type:



deposit\_type       is\_canceled

No Deposit         0.28

Non Refund         0.99

Refundable         0.22



So the Y-axis is the cancellation rate, where:



0.00 = 0% canceled

0.50 = 50% canceled

1.00 = 100% canceled



This is more appropriate than treating categorical values as numbers.



If you specifically want Y-axis literally labelled is\_canceled



Change:



ax.set\_ylabel("Cancellation Rate")



to:



ax.set\_ylabel("is\_canceled")



So your plots will visually show:



is\_canceled

&#x20;            |

&#x20;       1.0  |

&#x20;            |

&#x20;       0.5  |

&#x20;            |

&#x20;       0.0  |

&#x20;            +----------------

&#x20;                category



I recommend Cancellation Rate as the label, though, because the values are the mean of the binary is\_canceled variable, not individual 0/1 observations.

More importantly, your current dataframe has many columns stored as str even though they appear to be numeric, such as lead\_time, adults, adr, rating, etc.



1\. First convert the missing-value strings to actual NaN



For the whole dataframe:

If you also have "null" and "NA":

Now:



print(df.isna().sum())



will show the actual missing values.



2\. IterativeImputer only works with numeric data



Your dataframe currently has many str columns:



lead\_time                    str

arrival\_date\_year            str

adults                       str

children                     str

adr                          str

rating                       str



You cannot simply run IterativeImputer on the entire df.



For numeric columns, first convert them:

]



for col in numeric\_cols:

&#x20;   df\[col] = pd.to\_numeric(df\[col], errors="coerce")



Now those columns will be numeric.



3\. Apply IterativeImputer to numeric columns



from sklearn.experimental import enable\_iterative\_imputer

from sklearn.impute import IterativeImputer



imputer = IterativeImputer(

df\[numeric\_cols] = imputer.fit\_transform(df\[numeric\_cols])

Important: Don't use IterativeImputer for categorical columns

or:



from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer

&#x20;   strategy="most\_frequent"

)



Also: comment should generally not be imputed



Since your comment column contains free text, I would not use IterativeImputer on it.



Recommended structure for your dataframe



You effectively have three types:



Numeric

children

babies

adr

rating

...



→ IterativeImputer



Categorical



arrival\_date\_month

market\_segment

...



→ Most frequent / "unknown"



Free text



comment

import numpy as np



from sklearn.model\_selection import train\_test\_split

from sklearn.linear\_model import LogisticRegression

from sklearn.svm import LinearSVC

from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier



from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer

from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

def evaluate(

try:

if len(comment) > 5:

return " ".join(msg)



df\["generated\_comment"] = (

If Linear SVC is still too slow



For your dataset size, you don't really need to spend a long time optimizing Linear SVC if Logistic Regression or LightGBM can achieve a better score.



You can put a time-saving cap on Linear SVC:

&#x20;   class\_weight=class\_weight\_dict,

&#x20;   tol=1e-2,

&#x20;   dual=False

)



My preferred setting for your current pipeline



Use:

&#x20;   class\_weight=class\_weight\_dict,

&#x20;   max\_iter=500,

&#x20;   tol=1e-2,

&#x20;   dual=False

)



This gives you a fast benchmark for Linear SVC rather than allowing it to spend a very long time trying to fully converge.

bigram features

categorical one-hot features

selection.

&#x20;               "prep",

&#x20;           ),

&#x20;           (

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           )

&#x20;   }

&#x20;   # =========================================================

&#x20;   # EVALUATION HELPER

&#x20;   # =========================================================



&#x20;   def evaluate(model, X\_eval, y\_true, name, show\_report=True):



&#x20;       # -----------------------------------------------------

&#x20;       # PREDICTIONS

&#x20;       # -----------------------------------------------------



&#x20;       preds = model.predict(X\_eval)



&#x20;       f1 = f1\_score(

&#x20;           y\_true,

&#x20;           preds,

&#x20;           average="weighted"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       # -----------------------------------------------------

&#x20;       # ROC-AUC

&#x20;       # -----------------------------------------------------



&#x20;       try:



&#x20;           if hasattr(

&#x20;               model.named\_steps\["clf"],

&#x20;               "predict\_proba"

&#x20;           ):



&#x20;               probs = model.predict\_proba(

&#x20;                   X\_eval

&#x20;               )



&#x20;           else:



&#x20;               scores = model.decision\_function(

&#x20;                   X\_eval

&#x20;               )



&#x20;               scores = np.asarray(scores)



&#x20;               # Binary / multiclass safety

&#x20;               if scores.ndim == 1:

&#x20;                   scores = np.column\_stack(

&#x20;                       \[-scores, scores]

&#x20;                   )



&#x20;               exp = np.exp(

&#x20;                   scores -

&#x20;                   np.max(

&#x20;                       scores,

&#x20;                       axis=1,

&#x20;                       keepdims=True

&#x20;                   )

&#x20;               )



&#x20;               probs = exp / exp.sum(

&#x20;                   axis=1,

&#x20;                   keepdims=True

&#x20;               )



&#x20;           roc = roc\_auc\_score(

&#x20;               y\_true,

&#x20;               probs,

&#x20;               multi\_class="ovr",

&#x20;               average="weighted"

&#x20;           )



&#x20;       except Exception as e:



&#x20;           print(

&#x20;               f"\[WARNING] ROC-AUC failed for {name}: {e}"

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           roc = 0.0



&#x20;       # -----------------------------------------------------

&#x20;       # REPORT

&#x20;       # -----------------------------------------------------



&#x20;       if show\_report:



&#x20;           print("\\n==============================")

&#x20;           print(name)

&#x20;           print("==============================")



&#x20;           print(

&#x20;               classification\_report(

&#x20;                   y\_true,

&#x20;                   preds

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           print(

&#x20;               "F1 Score :",

&#x20;               round(f1, 4)

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           print(

&#x20;               "ROC-AUC  :",

&#x20;               round(roc, 4)

&#x20;           )



&#x20;       return {

&#x20;           "model": name,

&#x20;           "f1": f1,

&#x20;           "roc": roc

&#x20;       }



&#x20;   # =========================================================

&#x20;   # TRAIN MODELS

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # IMPORTANT:

&#x20;   # Only X\_train / y\_train are used for .fit()

&#x20;   # =========================================================



&#x20;   print("\\n==============================")

&#x20;   print("TRAINING MODELS")

&#x20;   print("==============================")



&#x20;   for name, model in models.items():



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           f"Training {name}..."

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       model.fit(

&#x20;           X\_train\_transformed,

&#x20;           y\_train

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       f"{name} completed."

&#x20;   )

\# =========================

\# =========================

\# PREDICT

\# =========================

def predict(self, x: dict):



&#x20;   structured\_features = \[

&#x20;       "comment",

&#x20;       "hotel",

&#x20;       "meal",

&#x20;       "market\_segment",

&#x20;       "distribution\_channel",

&#x20;       "deposit\_type",

&#x20;       "customer\_type",

&#x20;       "season\_group",

&#x20;       "country\_group",

&#x20;       "adr\_group",

&#x20;       "previous\_cancellations\_group",

&#x20;       "days\_in\_waiting\_list\_group",

&#x20;       "guest\_group",

&#x20;       "client\_segment",

&#x20;       "is\_top\_bad\_client",

&#x20;       "client\_bad\_rate"

&#x20;   ]



&#x20;   input\_df = pd.DataFrame(\[x])



&#x20;   for col in structured\_features:

&#x20;       if col not in input\_df:

&#x20;           input\_df\[col] = "unknown"



&#x20;   X\_input = input\_df\[structured\_features]



&#x20;   pred\_rating = int(self.best\_model.predict(X\_input)\[0])



&#x20;   clf = self.best\_model.named\_steps\["clf"]



\# =========================

&#x20;   # RESERVATION STATUS

&#x20;   #     PROBABILITY

&#x20;   # =========================



&#x20;   print(

&#x20;       "Calculating reservation status probabilities..."

&#x20;   )



status\_probs = (

&#x20;       status\_model.predict\_proba(

&#x20;           X\_all\_transformed

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



status\_class\_order = (

&#x20;       status\_model.classes\_

&#x20;   )



\# Create columns first

&#x20;   df\["prob\_canceled"] = 0.0

&#x20;   df\["prob\_check\_out"] = 0.0

&#x20;   df\["prob\_no\_show"] = 0.0



\# Map probability using

&#x20;   # actual class names

&#x20;   for i, cls in enumerate(

&#x20;       status\_class\_order

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       if cls == "canceled":



&#x20;           df\["prob\_canceled"] = (

&#x20;               status\_probs\[:, i] \*

&#x20;               100

&#x20;           )



&#x20;       elif cls == "check-out":



&#x20;           df\["prob\_check\_out"] = (

&#x20;               status\_probs\[:, i] \*

&#x20;               100

&#x20;           )



&#x20;       elif cls == "no-show":



&#x20;           df\["prob\_no\_show"] = (

&#x20;               status\_probs\[:, i] \*

&#x20;               100

&#x20;           )



\# Round probabilities

&#x20;   df\["prob\_canceled"] = (

&#x20;       df\["prob\_canceled"]

&#x20;       .round(1)

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   df\["prob\_check\_out"] = (

&#x20;       df\["prob\_check\_out"]

&#x20;       .round(1)

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   df\["prob\_no\_show"] = (

&#x20;       df\["prob\_no\_show"]

&#x20;       .round(1)

&#x20;   )



\# =========================

&#x20;   # SLA Risk

&#x20;   # =========================



if hasattr(clf, "predict\_proba"):

&#x20;       probs = self.best\_model.predict\_proba(X\_input)\[0]

&#x20;   else:

&#x20;       scores = self.best\_model.decision\_function(X\_input)

&#x20;       scores = np.asarray(scores)



&#x20;       if scores.ndim == 2:

&#x20;           scores = scores\[0]



&#x20;       exp = np.exp(scores - np.max(scores))

&#x20;       probs = exp / np.sum(exp)



&#x20;   class\_order = list(clf.classes\_)



&#x20;   risk\_weights = {0:1.0,1:0.9, 2:0.75, 3:0.6, 4:0.4, 5:0.2, 5:0.0}



&#x20;   sla\_risk = 0.0

&#x20;   for i, cls in enumerate(class\_order):

&#x20;       if i >= len(probs):

&#x20;           continue

&#x20;       sla\_risk += probs\[i] \* risk\_weights.get(cls, 0)



&#x20;   sla\_risk\_score = round(sla\_risk \* 100, 1)



&#x20;   rating\_map = {6:10, 5:20, 4:40, 3:60, 4:40, 5:20, 5:10}



&#x20;   base\_risk = rating\_map.get(pred\_rating, 50)



&#x20;   risk\_score = round(

&#x20;       0.6 \* base\_risk +

&#x20;       0.4 \* sla\_risk\_score,

&#x20;       1

&#x20;   )



generated\_comment = self.\_generate\_comment(

&#x20;       pred\_rating,

&#x20;       sla\_risk\_score,

&#x20;       risk\_score,

&#x20;       x

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   return (

&#x20;       pred\_rating,

&#x20;       "prob\_canceled",

&#x20;       "prob\_check\_out",

&#x20;       "prob\_no\_show",           

&#x20;       sla\_risk\_score,

&#x20;       risk\_score,

&#x20;       generated\_comment

&#x20;   )

&#x20;           "DataProcessor must be fitted before transform()"

&#x20;       )



df = df.copy()

&#x20;   df = self.\_lead\_time(df)



df = self.\_apply\_clientdriver\_behaviour(df)



&#x20;   df = self.\_apply\_bad\_clientdriver(df)



df = self.\_top\_comment(df)



df = self.\_apply\_top20\_comment(df)



print("FeatureEngineering transform completed")

def fit\_transform(self, train\_df):

\# =========================================================

\# Step 5 Feature Engineering 2

\# Lead time computation

\# =========================================================



def \_lead\_time(self, df):



\# ========================= 

&#x20;   # Family\_size computation

&#x20;   # =========================



\# Convert guest counts to numeric

&#x20;   df\["adults"] = pd.to\_numeric(df\["adults"], errors="coerce")

&#x20;   df\["children"] = pd.to\_numeric(df\["children"], errors="coerce")

&#x20;   df\["babies"] = pd.to\_numeric(df\["babies"], errors="coerce")



&#x20;   # Total number of guests

&#x20;   df\["total\_guests"] = (

&#x20;       df\["adults"].fillna(0)

&#x20;       + df\["children"].fillna(0)

&#x20;       + df\["babies"].fillna(0)

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   # Group guests

&#x20;   df\["guest\_group"] = np.select(

&#x20;       \[

&#x20;           # Single adult

&#x20;           (df\["adults"] == 1) \&

&#x20;           (df\["children"] == 0) \&

&#x20;           (df\["babies"] == 0),



&#x20;           # Couple

&#x20;           (df\["adults"] == 2) \&

&#x20;           (df\["children"] == 0) \&

&#x20;           (df\["babies"] == 0),



&#x20;           # Family

&#x20;           (df\["children"] > 0) |

&#x20;           (df\["babies"] > 0),



&#x20;           # Larger group

&#x20;           (df\["adults"] >= 3) \&

&#x20;           (df\["children"] == 0) \&

&#x20;           (df\["babies"] == 0)

&#x20;       ],

&#x20;       \[

&#x20;           "Single",

&#x20;           "Couple",

&#x20;           "Family",

&#x20;           "Group"

&#x20;       ],

&#x20;       default="Unknown"

&#x20;   )



print("Pre-process - Lead time \& Service Level Computation")

&#x20;   return df

\# =========================================================



def \_fit\_clientdriver\_behaviour(self, df):



&#x20;   # Client average rating

&#x20;   self.client\_stats = (

&#x20;       df.groupby("client\_email")\["final\_rating"]

&#x20;       .mean()

&#x20;       .reset\_index()

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   self.client\_stats.columns = \[

&#x20;       "client\_email",

&#x20;       "client\_avg\_rating"

&#x20;   ]



def client\_label(r):



&#x20;       if r <= 2:

&#x20;           return "Client - bad review"



&#x20;       elif r == 3:

&#x20;           return "Client - neutral review"



&#x20;       else:

&#x20;           return "Client - good review"



self.client\_stats\["client\_segment"] = (

&#x20;       self.client\_stats\["client\_avg\_rating"]

&#x20;       .apply(client\_label)

&#x20;   )



print("Feature Engineering - Client \& Driver Statistics fitted")



\# =========================================================

\# Step 5.3 Client \& Driver Behaviour - TRANSFORM

\# =========================================================



def \_apply\_clientdriver\_behaviour(self, df):



&#x20;   df = df.merge(

&#x20;       self.client\_stats\[

&#x20;           \[

&#x20;               "client\_email",

&#x20;               "client\_segment"

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;       ],

&#x20;       on="client\_email",

&#x20;       how="left"

&#x20;   )



df\["client\_segment"] = (

&#x20;       df\["client\_segment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("Client - unknown")

&#x20;   )



return df

\# =========================================================



def \_fit\_bad\_clientdriver(self, df):



&#x20;   df = df.copy()



df\["is\_bad\_rating"] = (

&#x20;       df\["final\_rating"]

&#x20;       .isin(\[0, 1, 2])

&#x20;       .astype(int)

&#x20;   )



\# -------------------------

&#x20;   # Client bad rate

&#x20;   # -------------------------



&#x20;   self.client\_bad\_stats = (

&#x20;       df.groupby("client\_email")

&#x20;       .agg(

&#x20;           total=("final\_rating", "count"),

&#x20;           bad\_count=("is\_bad\_rating", "sum")

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       .reset\_index()

&#x20;   )



self.client\_bad\_stats\["client\_bad\_rate"] = (

&#x20;       self.client\_bad\_stats\["bad\_count"]

&#x20;       /

&#x20;       self.client\_bad\_stats\["total"]

&#x20;   )



top\_10\_bad\_clients = (

&#x20;       self.client\_bad\_stats

&#x20;       .sort\_values(

&#x20;           "client\_bad\_rate",

&#x20;           ascending=False

&#x20;       )    

&#x20;       .head(10)

&#x20;   )



self.top\_bad\_clients = (

&#x20;       top\_10\_bad\_clients\["client\_email"]

&#x20;       .tolist()

&#x20;   )



print("Feature Engineering - Bad Client Driver Statistics fitted")



\# =========================================================

\# Step 5.4 Bad Client \& Driver - TRANSFORM

\# =========================================================



def \_apply\_bad\_clientdriver(self, df):



&#x20;   df = df.copy()



df = df.merge(

&#x20;       self.client\_bad\_stats\[

&#x20;           \[

&#x20;               "client\_email",

&#x20;               "client\_bad\_rate"

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;       ],

&#x20;       on="client\_email",

&#x20;       how="left"

&#x20;   )



df\["client\_bad\_rate"] = (

&#x20;       df\["client\_bad\_rate"]

&#x20;       .fillna(0)

&#x20;   )



df\["is\_top\_bad\_client"] = (

&#x20;       df\["client\_email"]

&#x20;       .isin(self.top\_bad\_clients)

&#x20;       .astype(int)

&#x20;   )



\# Store for UI

&#x20;   df.attrs\["top\_10\_bad\_clients"] = (

&#x20;       self.top\_bad\_clients

&#x20;   )



return df

\# =========================================================

\# Step 5.6 Top Comment Clustering - FIT

\# =========================================================



def \_fit\_top20\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   import re

&#x20;   import numpy as np



&#x20;   from sentence\_transformers import SentenceTransformer

&#x20;   from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 FIT Comment Clustering"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 1. ONLY BAD REVIEWS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\_bad = df\[

&#x20;       df\["final\_rating"] <= 3

&#x20;   ].copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 2. CLEAN COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\_bad\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;       .str.lower()

&#x20;   )



def clean\_text(text):



&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'ðÿ\\S\*', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\[^a-z0-9\\s]', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text)



&#x20;       return text.strip()



df\_bad\["comment\_clean"] = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment"]

&#x20;       .apply(clean\_text)

&#x20;   )



\# Remove empty comments

&#x20;   df\_bad = df\_bad\[

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment\_clean"].str.len() > 0

&#x20;   ].copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 3. COUNT COMMENT FREQUENCY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   comment\_counts = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment\_clean"]

&#x20;       .value\_counts()

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 4. TOP 20 COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   top20\_comments = (

&#x20;       comment\_counts

&#x20;       .head(20)

&#x20;   )



if top20\_comments.empty:



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           "Step 5.6 - No valid bad-review comments found"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model = None

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_samples = {}

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_labels = {}

&#x20;       self.top20\_comments = \[]



&#x20;       return



self.top20\_comments = (

&#x20;       top20\_comments.index.tolist()

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Top "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.top20\_comments)} comments selected"

&#x20;   )



for i, comment in enumerate(

&#x20;       self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;       start=1

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           f"  {i:02d}. "

&#x20;           f"{comment} "

&#x20;           f"(count={top20\_comments\[comment]})"

&#x20;       )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 5. SENTENCE TRANSFORMER

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   print(

&#x20;       "Step 5.6 - Loading SentenceTransformer..."

&#x20;   )



self.comment\_embedding\_model = (

&#x20;       SentenceTransformer(

&#x20;           "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 6. EMBED TOP 20 COMMENTS ONLY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   embeddings = (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model.encode(

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           convert\_to\_numpy=True,

&#x20;           normalize\_embeddings=True,

&#x20;           batch\_size=20,

&#x20;           show\_progress\_bar=False

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Generated embeddings for "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.top20\_comments)} comments"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 7. CREATE 10 CLUSTERS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   n\_clusters = min(

&#x20;       10,

&#x20;       len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;   )



if n\_clusters == 1:



&#x20;       clusters = np.zeros(

&#x20;           len(self.top20\_comments),

&#x20;           dtype=int

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   else:



&#x20;       cluster\_model = (

&#x20;           AgglomerativeClustering(

&#x20;               n\_clusters=n\_clusters,

&#x20;               metric="cosine",

&#x20;               linkage="average"

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       clusters = (

&#x20;           cluster\_model.fit\_predict(

&#x20;               embeddings

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 8. STORE CLUSTER LABELS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   self.comment\_cluster\_labels = dict(

&#x20;       zip(

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           clusters

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 9. STORE CLUSTER CENTROIDS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}



self.comment\_cluster\_samples = {}



for cluster\_id in sorted(

&#x20;       set(clusters)

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       cluster\_mask = (

&#x20;           clusters == cluster\_id

&#x20;       )



cluster\_embeddings = (

&#x20;           embeddings\[

&#x20;               cluster\_mask

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;       )



\# Mean embedding

&#x20;       centroid = (

&#x20;           cluster\_embeddings

&#x20;           .mean(axis=0)

&#x20;       )



\# Normalize centroid

&#x20;       centroid\_norm = np.linalg.norm(

&#x20;           centroid

&#x20;       )



if centroid\_norm > 0:



&#x20;           centroid = (

&#x20;               centroid /

&#x20;               centroid\_norm

&#x20;           )



self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;           cluster\_id

&#x20;       ] = centroid



\# ---------------------------------------------

&#x20;       # Store sample comments

&#x20;       # ---------------------------------------------



&#x20;       cluster\_comments = \[

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments\[i]

&#x20;           for i in range(

&#x20;               len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;           )

&#x20;           if clusters\[i] == cluster\_id

&#x20;       ]



self.comment\_cluster\_samples\[

&#x20;           cluster\_id

&#x20;       ] = cluster\_comments\[:3]



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - "

&#x20;       "Step 5.6 FIT Top Comment Clustering completed"

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.comment\_cluster\_centroids)} clusters created"

&#x20;   )



\# =========================================================

\# Step 5.6 Top Comment Clustering - APPLY

\# =========================================================



def \_apply\_top20\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   import re

&#x20;   import numpy as np



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 APPLY Comment Clustering"

&#x20;   )



df = df.copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 1. CLEAN COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;       .str.lower()

&#x20;   )



def clean\_text(text):



&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'ðÿ\\S\*', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\[^a-z0-9\\s]', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text)



&#x20;       return text.strip()



df\["comment\_clean"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .apply(clean\_text)

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 2. CHECK WHETHER MODEL EXISTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   if (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model is None

&#x20;       or not self.comment\_cluster\_centroids

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       df\["cluster"] = -1



&#x20;       df\["business\_categories"] = (

&#x20;           "Other / Acceptable Service"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       df\["sample\_comments"] = None



&#x20;       return df



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 3. UNIQUE NON-EMPTY COMMENTS ONLY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   unique\_comments = (

&#x20;       df.loc\[

&#x20;           df\["comment\_clean"].str.len() > 0,

&#x20;           "comment\_clean"

&#x20;       ]

&#x20;       .drop\_duplicates()

&#x20;       .tolist()

&#x20;   )



if not unique\_comments:



&#x20;       df\["cluster"] = -1



&#x20;       df\["business\_categories"] = (

&#x20;           "Other / Acceptable Service"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       df\["sample\_comments"] = None



&#x20;       return df



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Applying clustering to "

&#x20;       f"{len(unique\_comments):,} unique comments "

&#x20;       f"from {len(df):,} rows"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 4. EMBED UNIQUE COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   embeddings = (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model.encode(

&#x20;           unique\_comments,

&#x20;           convert\_to\_numpy=True,

&#x20;           normalize\_embeddings=True,

&#x20;           batch\_size=64,

&#x20;           show\_progress\_bar=False

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 5. BUILD CENTROID MATRIX

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   cluster\_ids = list(

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_centroids.keys()

&#x20;   )



centroid\_matrix = np.vstack(

&#x20;       \[

&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;               cluster\_id

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;           for cluster\_id in cluster\_ids

&#x20;       ]

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 6. COSINE SIMILARITY

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # Both embeddings and centroids are normalized.

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # Therefore:

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # cosine similarity

&#x20;   # =

&#x20;   # dot product

&#x20;   # =====================================================

def \_fit\_bad\_clientdriver(self, df):

self.top\_bad\_clients = (

\# =========================================================

\# Step 5.6 Top Comment Clustering - FIT

\# =========================================================



def \_fit\_top20\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   import re

&#x20;   import numpy as np



&#x20;   from sentence\_transformers import SentenceTransformer

&#x20;   from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 FIT Comment Clustering"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 1. ONLY BAD REVIEWS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\_bad = df\[

&#x20;       df\["final\_rating"] <= 3

&#x20;   ].copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 2. CLEAN COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\_bad\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;       .str.lower()

&#x20;   )



def clean\_text(text):



&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'ðÿ\\S\*', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\[^a-z0-9\\s]', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text)



&#x20;       return text.strip()



df\_bad\["comment\_clean"] = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment"]

&#x20;       .apply(clean\_text)

&#x20;   )



\# Remove empty comments

&#x20;   df\_bad = df\_bad\[

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment\_clean"].str.len() > 0

&#x20;   ].copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 3. COUNT COMMENT FREQUENCY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   comment\_counts = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment\_clean"]

&#x20;       .value\_counts()

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 4. TOP 20 COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   top20\_comments = (

&#x20;       comment\_counts

&#x20;       .head(20)

&#x20;   )



if top20\_comments.empty:



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           "Step 5.6 - No valid bad-review comments found"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model = None

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_samples = {}

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_labels = {}

&#x20;       self.top20\_comments = \[]



&#x20;       return



self.top20\_comments = (

&#x20;       top20\_comments.index.tolist()

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Top "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.top20\_comments)} comments selected"

&#x20;   )



for i, comment in enumerate(

&#x20;       self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;       start=1

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           f"  {i:02d}. "

&#x20;           f"{comment} "

&#x20;           f"(count={top20\_comments\[comment]})"

&#x20;       )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 5. SENTENCE TRANSFORMER

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   print(

&#x20;       "Step 5.6 - Loading SentenceTransformer..."

&#x20;   )



self.comment\_embedding\_model = (

&#x20;       SentenceTransformer(

&#x20;           "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 6. EMBED TOP 20 COMMENTS ONLY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   embeddings = (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model.encode(

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           convert\_to\_numpy=True,

&#x20;           normalize\_embeddings=True,

&#x20;           batch\_size=20,

&#x20;           show\_progress\_bar=False

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Generated embeddings for "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.top20\_comments)} comments"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 7. CREATE 10 CLUSTERS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   n\_clusters = min(

&#x20;       10,

&#x20;       len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;   )



if n\_clusters == 1:



&#x20;       clusters = np.zeros(

&#x20;           len(self.top20\_comments),

&#x20;           dtype=int

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   else:



&#x20;       cluster\_model = (

&#x20;           AgglomerativeClustering(

&#x20;               n\_clusters=n\_clusters,

&#x20;               metric="cosine",

&#x20;               linkage="average"

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       clusters = (

&#x20;           cluster\_model.fit\_predict(

&#x20;               embeddings

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 8. STORE CLUSTER LABELS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   self.comment\_cluster\_labels = dict(

&#x20;       zip(

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           clusters

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 9. STORE CLUSTER CENTROIDS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}



self.comment\_cluster\_samples = {}



for cluster\_id in sorted(

&#x20;       set(clusters)

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       cluster\_mask = (

&#x20;           clusters == cluster\_id

&#x20;       )



cluster\_embeddings = (

&#x20;           embeddings\[

&#x20;               cluster\_mask

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;       )



\# Mean embedding

&#x20;       centroid = (

&#x20;           cluster\_embeddings

&#x20;           .mean(axis=0)

&#x20;       )



\# Normalize centroid

&#x20;       centroid\_norm = np.linalg.norm(

&#x20;           centroid

&#x20;       )



if centroid\_norm > 0:



&#x20;           centroid = (

&#x20;               centroid /

&#x20;               centroid\_norm

&#x20;           )



self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;           cluster\_id

&#x20;       ] = centroid



\# ---------------------------------------------

&#x20;       # Store sample comments

&#x20;       # ---------------------------------------------



&#x20;       cluster\_comments = \[

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments\[i]

&#x20;           for i in range(

&#x20;               len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;           )

&#x20;           if clusters\[i] == cluster\_id

&#x20;       ]



self.comment\_cluster\_samples\[

&#x20;           cluster\_id

&#x20;       ] = cluster\_comments\[:3]



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - "

&#x20;       "Step 5.6 FIT Top Comment Clustering completed"

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.comment\_cluster\_centroids)} clusters created"

&#x20;   )

\# Step 5.6 Top Comment Clustering - APPLY

\# =========================================================



def \_apply\_top20\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   import re

&#x20;   import numpy as np



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 APPLY Comment Clustering"

&#x20;   )



df = df.copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 1. CLEAN COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;       .str.lower()

&#x20;   )



def clean\_text(text):



&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'ðÿ\\S\*', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\[^a-z0-9\\s]', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text)



&#x20;       return text.strip()



df\["comment\_clean"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .apply(clean\_text)

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 2. CHECK WHETHER MODEL EXISTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   if (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model is None

&#x20;       or not self.comment\_cluster\_centroids

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       df\["cluster"] = -1



&#x20;       df\["business\_categories"] = (

&#x20;           "Other / Acceptable Service"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       df\["sample\_comments"] = None



&#x20;       return df



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 3. UNIQUE NON-EMPTY COMMENTS ONLY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   unique\_comments = (

&#x20;       df.loc\[

&#x20;           df\["comment\_clean"].str.len() > 0,

&#x20;           "comment\_clean"

&#x20;       ]

&#x20;       .drop\_duplicates()

&#x20;       .tolist()

&#x20;   )



if not unique\_comments:



&#x20;       df\["cluster"] = -1



&#x20;       df\["business\_categories"] = (

&#x20;           "Other / Acceptable Service"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       df\["sample\_comments"] = None



&#x20;       return df



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Applying clustering to "

&#x20;       f"{len(unique\_comments):,} unique comments "

&#x20;       f"from {len(df):,} rows"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 4. EMBED UNIQUE COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   embeddings = (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model.encode(

&#x20;           unique\_comments,

&#x20;           convert\_to\_numpy=True,

&#x20;           normalize\_embeddings=True,

&#x20;           batch\_size=64,

&#x20;           show\_progress\_bar=False

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 5. BUILD CENTROID MATRIX

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   cluster\_ids = list(

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_centroids.keys()

&#x20;   )



centroid\_matrix = np.vstack(

&#x20;       \[

&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;               cluster\_id

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;           for cluster\_id in cluster\_ids

&#x20;       ]

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 6. COSINE SIMILARITY

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # Both embeddings and centroids are normalized.

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # Therefore:

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # cosine similarity

&#x20;   # =

&#x20;   # dot product

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   similarity\_matrix = (

&#x20;       embeddings @ centroid\_matrix.T

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 7. FIND BEST CLUSTER

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   best\_cluster\_indices = (

&#x20;       np.argmax(

&#x20;           similarity\_matrix,

&#x20;           axis=1

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



unique\_cluster\_labels = \[

&#x20;       cluster\_ids\[index]

&#x20;       for index in best\_cluster\_indices

&#x20;   ]



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 8. COMMENT -> CLUSTER LOOKUP

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   comment\_to\_cluster = dict(

&#x20;       zip(

&#x20;           unique\_comments,

&#x20;           unique\_cluster\_labels

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



df\["cluster"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment\_clean"]

&#x20;       .map(

&#x20;           comment\_to\_cluster

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       .fillna(-1)

&#x20;       .astype(int)

&#x20;   )

client 2 → scan 118k rows

client 3 → scan 118k rows

...

client N → scan 118k rows

Yes — and this is important. Your current FeatureEngineer.fit() structure can create data leakage if the same fitted statistics/models are later applied to train, test, and actual prediction data.



The good news is that your intended structure can be made leakage-safe.



What the recommended structure changes



The key principle should be:



RAW TRAIN DATA

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

DataProcessor.fit(train)

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ├── learns encoders

&#x20;    ├── learns rating model

&#x20;    └── learns imputer

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

DataProcessor.transform(train)

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

FeatureEngineer.fit(train)

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ├── learns client statistics

&#x20;    ├── learns bad-client statistics

&#x20;    ├── learns top comments

&#x20;    └── learns comment clustering

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

FeatureEngineer.transform(train)

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

TRAIN MODEL



Then:



RAW TEST DATA

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

DataProcessor.transform(test)

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

FeatureEngineer.transform(test)

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

MODEL.predict(test)



And actual/new data:



RAW ACTUAL DATA

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

DataProcessor.transform(actual)

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

FeatureEngineer.transform(actual)

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

MODEL.predict(actual)



Never call .fit() or .fit\_transform() on test or actual data.



1\. The biggest issue in your current code



This is currently inside:



def fit(self, train\_df):



&#x20;   df = train\_df.copy()



&#x20;   df = self.\_business\_rules(df)

&#x20;   df = self.\_lead\_time(df)



&#x20;   self.\_fit\_clientdriver\_behaviour(df)



&#x20;   self.\_fit\_bad\_clientdriver(df)



&#x20;   df = self.\_apply\_clientdriver\_behaviour(df)



&#x20;   df = self.\_apply\_bad\_clientdriver(df)



&#x20;   df = self.\_top\_comment(df)



&#x20;   self.\_fit\_top20\_comment(df)



&#x20;   df = self.\_apply\_top20\_comment(df)



The problem is that some things are being learned from the entire training dataset before your eventual train/test split, depending on where you split.



For example:



self.client\_stats = (

&#x20;   df.groupby("client\_email")\["final\_rating"]

&#x20;   .mean()

)



This learns client average rating.



And:



self.client\_bad\_stats = (

&#x20;   df.groupby("client\_email")

&#x20;   .agg(...)

)



This learns client bad-rating history.



And:



comment\_counts = (

&#x20;   df\_bad\["comment\_clean"]

&#x20;   .value\_counts()

)



This learns which comments are most frequent.



Then:



self.comment\_embedding\_model



and clustering are learned from those selected comments.



If you do:



split train/test

&#x20;      ↓

FeatureEngineer.fit(full dataset)

&#x20;      ↓

train/test



then test information has already entered the FeatureEngineer.



That is leakage.



2\. Correct order



You should split before fitting anything that learns from data.



For example:



train\_df, test\_df = train\_test\_split(

&#x20;   df,

&#x20;   test\_size=0.2,

&#x20;   random\_state=42,

&#x20;   stratify=df\["final\_rating"]

)



Then:



TRAIN



processor.fit(train\_df)



train\_processed = processor.transform(train\_df)



feature\_engineer.fit(train\_processed)



train\_features = feature\_engineer.transform(

&#x20;   train\_processed

)



TEST



test\_processed = processor.transform(test\_df)



test\_features = feature\_engineer.transform(

&#x20;   test\_processed

)



Notice:



processor.fit(test\_df)



NO



and:



feature\_engineer.fit(test\_processed)



NO



3\. Your rating model also needs this treatment



Your current:



def \_fit\_rating\_model(self, df):



&#x20;   train = df\[df\["rating"].notna()]



&#x20;   X = train\["comment"].fillna("")

&#x20;   y = train\["rating"].astype(int)



&#x20;   self.rating\_model.fit(X, y)



is okay provided DataProcessor.fit() receives only the training split.



For example:



FULL DATA

&#x20;  │

&#x20;  ├── 80% TRAIN ──→ rating model learns here

&#x20;  │

&#x20;  └── 20% TEST



The rating model must never see test comments or test ratings during fitting.



4\. Your 0–6 rating requirement



You previously clarified:



Rating:

0

1

2

3

4

5

6



And:



Bad rating:

0

1

2



So your bad-review logic should consistently be:



df\["is\_bad\_rating"] = (

&#x20;   df\["final\_rating"].isin(\[0, 1, 2])

&#x20;   .astype(int)

)



That's correct.



But I see another problem in your current clustering code:



df\_bad = df\[

&#x20;   df\["final\_rating"] <= 3

].copy()



That means rating 3 is being treated as a bad review.



If your definition is:



0–2 = Bad

3   = Neutral

4–6 = Good



then this should be:



df\_bad = df\[

&#x20;   df\["final\_rating"].isin(\[0, 1, 2])

].copy()



This is important.



Otherwise your dashboard/model will have inconsistent definitions:



Bad statistics     → 0,1,2

Comment clustering → 0,1,2,3



You should make both use exactly the same rule.



5\. Another important leakage issue: client statistics



Suppose you have:



Client A



Booking 1 → rating 6

Booking 2 → rating 5

Booking 3 → rating 1

Booking 4 → rating 0



If Booking 4 is in the test set, but you calculate:



client\_avg\_rating



using all four bookings, then Booking 4's own rating contributes to the feature used to predict Booking 4.



That's leakage.



Even worse, if the client has many test records, test information gets incorporated into:



client\_avg\_rating

client\_bad\_rate



6\. For your project, there are actually TWO levels of leakage



This is the important part.



Level 1 — train/test leakage



You must prevent:



TEST

&#x20;↓

FeatureEngineer.fit()

&#x20;↓

TRAINING



Simple solution:



Split first, fit second.



Level 2 — target leakage



Your features themselves must not use the target you're trying to predict.



For example, if your model predicts:



reservation\_status



then a feature cannot be calculated using information that only exists after the reservation outcome.



Likewise, if the model predicts:



final\_rating



you cannot create a feature using:



client\_avg\_rating

client\_bad\_rate



calculated from ratings that include the current observation.



That's target leakage.



7\. Your final\_rating needs special consideration



You currently do:



result\["rating"] = df\["rating"]

result\["final\_rating"] = df\["final\_rating"]



That's fine for the preprocessing pipeline if rating is a known input/target, but you need to decide what your ML model is actually predicting.



If:



final\_rating = TARGET



then final\_rating must not be passed as an input feature to a model predicting final rating.



Likewise:



rating

rating\_predicted

final\_rating



should be carefully separated into:



TARGET



versus:



FEATURES

&#x20;                TRAIN / TEST SPLIT

&#x20;                    80%      20%

&#x20;                      │        │

&#x20;                      │        │

&#x20;                      ▼        │

&#x20;             DataProcessor.fit()

&#x20;                      │

&#x20;                      ▼

&#x20;          DataProcessor.transform()

&#x20;                      │

&#x20;                      ▼

&#x20;            FeatureEngineer.fit()

&#x20;                      │

&#x20;                      ▼

&#x20;         FeatureEngineer.transform()

&#x20;                      │

&#x20;                      ▼

&#x20;                MODEL TRAINING

Yes. Looking at your actual model.py together with feature\_engineering.py, there is an important issue:



Your model.py train/test split itself is mostly correct, but data leakage has already happened before model.py performs the split.



This is because app.py currently does approximately:



feature\_engineer.fit\_transform(df)

service\_model.train(df)



So by the time ServiceModel.train() receives df, the feature engineering has already learned from all 118,196 rows, including rows that later become validation/test.



That matters much more than the train/test split code inside model.py.



1\. Where your current leakage occurs



Your current flow is effectively:



RAW HOTEL DATABASE

&#x20;      │

&#x20;      ▼

DataProcessor.fit\_transform(ALL DATA)

&#x20;      │

&#x20;      ▼

FeatureEngineer.fit\_transform(ALL DATA)

&#x20;      │

&#x20;      ├── client statistics ← ALL DATA

&#x20;      ├── bad client statistics ← ALL DATA

&#x20;      ├── top comments ← ALL DATA

&#x20;      └── comment clustering ← ALL DATA

&#x20;      │

&#x20;      ▼

ServiceModel.train()

&#x20;      │

&#x20;      ▼

Split into

Train 80%

Validation 10%

Test 10%



The problem is:



┌───────────────────┐

&#x20;                │  ALL 118,196 rows │

&#x20;                └─────────┬─────────┘

&#x20;                          │

&#x20;                 FeatureEngineer

&#x20;                          │

&#x20;             learns information from

&#x20;                  test/validation

&#x20;                          │

&#x20;                          ▼

&#x20;               THEN split the data



So the test set is not truly unseen.



2\. Specific leakage in your feature\_engineering.py



These are the important ones.



A. client\_segment



You currently do:



self.client\_stats = (

&#x20;   df.groupby("client\_email")\["final\_rating"]

&#x20;   .mean()

&#x20;   .reset\_index()

)



This uses:



final\_rating



from the entire dataset.



Suppose:



Client A



TRAIN:

rating = 6

rating = 6



TEST:

rating = 1



Your current feature engineer calculates:



Client A average = (6 + 6 + 1) / 3

&#x20;               = 4.33



Then the training rows get:



Client A → good



and the test row has also influenced that calculation.



That is leakage.



3\. client\_bad\_rate is also leakage



You calculate:



df\["is\_bad\_rating"] = (

&#x20;   df\["final\_rating"]

&#x20;   .isin(\[0, 1, 2])

&#x20;   .astype(int)

)



Then:



self.client\_bad\_stats = (

&#x20;   df.groupby("client\_email")

&#x20;   .agg(

&#x20;       total=("final\_rating", "count"),

&#x20;       bad\_count=("is\_bad\_rating", "sum")

&#x20;   )

&#x20;   .reset\_index()

)



Again, this uses the target:



final\_rating



from the entire dataset.



Therefore:



client\_bad\_rate



contains information about the target.



This is one of the strongest leakage sources in your project.



4\. top\_bad\_clients is also leakage



You do:



top\_10\_bad\_clients = (

&#x20;   self.client\_bad\_stats

&#x20;   .sort\_values(

&#x20;       "client\_bad\_rate",

&#x20;       ascending=False

&#x20;   )

&#x20;   .head(10)

)



This means you identify the "worst clients" using all ratings, including test ratings.



Then:



df\["is\_top\_bad\_client"] = (

&#x20;   df\["client\_email"]

&#x20;   .isin(self.top\_bad\_clients)

&#x20;   .astype(int)

)



So the test set influences the feature:



is\_top\_bad\_client



Again, leakage.



5\. Your comment topic model leaks too



This part in model.py is another major issue:



comment\_tfidf = tfidf.fit\_transform(

&#x20;   df\["comment"]

)



comment\_features\_array = svd.fit\_transform(

&#x20;   comment\_tfidf

)



This occurs before the train/test split.



So:



TF-IDF vocabulary

&#x20;       +

SVD topic structure



is learned from:



TRAIN

\+

VALIDATION

\+

TEST



Then you split the data.



That's technically leakage.



It may not be as severe as directly using final\_rating, but it violates the clean ML rule:



Anything that learns parameters from the data must be fitted using training data only.



6\. Your \_top\_comment() also uses the entire dataset



This:



for r in df\["final\_rating"].unique():

10\. But there is an additional issue with your client statistics



There is an important question:



Should client\_avg\_rating use final\_rating?



Currently:



client\_avg\_rating



is calculated from:



final\_rating



If your prediction target is:



final\_rating



then this is target leakage by design.



For example:



client\_bad\_rate

client\_avg\_rating

client\_segment



are all derived from the thing you are trying to predict.



Even if you calculate them using TRAIN only, they can still create target-derived features.



There are two approaches.



Safer approach



Do not use:



client\_avg\_rating

client\_segment

client\_bad\_rate

is\_top\_bad\_client



as predictive features for final\_rating.



Use them only for:



dashboard analytics

historical customer profiling



More advanced approach



You can retain historical client statistics if you specifically want a "historical behaviour" model, but you must calculate them using past observations only, not the current observation's target.



That requires a temporal/ordered feature-engineering strategy.



For your current assessment, I would recommend the safer approach.

You need to distinguish:

from:

For actual prediction, only booking-time information should be available.

Yes. I checked model.py against the revised app.py, and there are several critical inconsistencies that will cause errors or, worse, incorrect training.



The biggest issue is that app.py now performs the train/validation/test split, while model.py still contains its own split logic and also has several undefined variables.



Critical problems I found



for data in \[...] has no body → IndentationError.



df is used but never defined inside train().



comment\_tfidf is referenced but the variable created is train\_comment\_tfidf.



Validation/test TF-IDF incorrectly use fit\_transform() on training data.



SVD is incorrectly fitted again for validation/test.



comment\_features\_array is undefined.



df.index is used although df is undefined.



ServiceModel.train() is being passed train\_df, val\_df, test\_df from app.py, but the model code tries to split again.



status\_model and X\_all\_transformed in predict() are undefined.



df, prob\_canceled, prob\_check\_out, prob\_no\_show in predict() are undefined.



Hotel structured features in model.py don't match the structured\_features list in app.py.



app.py expects a saved ServiceModel containing best\_model, so the artifact handling needs to remain consistent.



Risk mappings contain incorrect/duplicate rating keys in predict().



self.\_save\_artifacts(df) saves the model again, while app.py assumes service\_model\_path is the service model artifact.



Most importantly, the comment-topic model must be fit only on train\_df and then transformed on validation/test/actual dashboard data. This preserves the leakage-free pipeline.



Because your revised app.py already does the split, I recommend making model.py accept those three datasets directly and not split again.

\# =========================================================

&#x20;       # ATTACH COMMENT FEATURES

\# =========================================================

&#x20;       # EVALUATION HELPER

&#x20;       # =========================================================



&#x20;       def evaluate(

&#x20;           model,

&#x20;           X\_eval,

&#x20;           y\_true,

&#x20;           name,

&#x20;           show\_report=True

&#x20;       ):



&#x20;           preds = model.predict(

&#x20;               X\_eval

&#x20;           )



f1 = f1\_score(

&#x20;               y\_true,

&#x20;               preds,

&#x20;               average="weighted"

&#x20;           )



try:



&#x20;               clf = model.named\_steps\[

&#x20;                   "clf"

&#x20;               ]



if hasattr(

&#x20;                   clf,

&#x20;                   "predict\_proba"

&#x20;               ):



&#x20;                   probs = model.predict\_proba(

&#x20;                       X\_eval

&#x20;                   )



&#x20;               else:



&#x20;                   scores = model.decision\_function(

&#x20;                       X\_eval

&#x20;                   )



&#x20;                   scores = np.asarray(

&#x20;                       scores

&#x20;                   )



if scores.ndim == 1:



&#x20;                       scores = np.column\_stack(

&#x20;                           \[

&#x20;                               -scores,

&#x20;                               scores

&#x20;                           ]

&#x20;                       )



exp = np.exp(

&#x20;                       scores -

&#x20;                       np.max(

&#x20;                           scores,

&#x20;                           axis=1,

&#x20;                           keepdims=True

&#x20;                       )

&#x20;                   )



probs = (

&#x20;                       exp /

&#x20;                       exp.sum(

&#x20;                           axis=1,

&#x20;                           keepdims=True

&#x20;                       )

&#x20;                   )



roc = roc\_auc\_score(

&#x20;                   y\_true,

&#x20;                   probs,

&#x20;                   multi\_class="ovr",

&#x20;                   average="weighted"

&#x20;               )



except Exception as e:



&#x20;               print(

&#x20;                   f"\[WARNING] ROC-AUC failed "

&#x20;                   f"for {name}: {e}"

&#x20;               )



&#x20;               roc = 0.0



if show\_report:



&#x20;               print()

&#x20;               print("==============================")

&#x20;               print(name)

&#x20;               print("==============================")



print(

&#x20;                   classification\_report(

&#x20;                       y\_true,

&#x20;                       preds

&#x20;                   )

&#x20;               )



print(

&#x20;                   "F1 Score :",

&#x20;                   round(

&#x20;                       f1,

&#x20;                       4

&#x20;                   )

&#x20;               )



print(

&#x20;                   "ROC-AUC  :",

&#x20;                   round(

&#x20;                       roc,

&#x20;                       4

&#x20;                   )

&#x20;               )



return {



&#x20;               "model": name,

&#x20;               "f1": f1,

&#x20;               "roc": roc



&#x20;           }

&#x20;       # TRAIN MODELS

One important point about app.py



There is still one error in the app.py you posted that must be fixed alongside this model.py.



You currently have:



train\_df, temp\_df = train\_test\_split(

&#x20;   training\_df,



but training\_df does not exist.



You loaded:



df = load\_data(

&#x20;   CONFIG

)



So the clean approach is:



raw\_training\_df = load\_data(

&#x20;   CONFIG

)



print(

&#x20;   f"\[INFO] Training data shape: "

&#x20;   f"{raw\_training\_df.shape}"

)



Then:



train\_df, temp\_df = train\_test\_split(

&#x20;   raw\_training\_df,

&#x20;   test\_size=0.20,

&#x20;   random\_state=42,

&#x20;   stratify=raw\_training\_df\["final\_rating"]

)



val\_df, test\_df = train\_test\_split(

&#x20;   temp\_df,

&#x20;   test\_size=0.50,

&#x20;   random\_state=42,

&#x20;   stratify=temp\_df\["final\_rating"]

)



However, there is an architectural issue here that is important for your leakage-free requirement:



Your current app.py split happens before DataProcessor



That is correct only if DataProcessor is fitted on train\_df and then transformed on val\_df/test\_df.



Your current app.py then does:



train\_df = processor.fit\_transform(train\_df)



val\_df = processor.transform(val\_df)



test\_df = processor.transform(test\_df)



That is good.



Then model.py receives:



service\_model.train(

&#x20;   train\_df,

&#x20;   val\_df,

&#x20;   test\_df

)



So the corrected model.py above does not split again.



The resulting pipeline is:



RAW DATABASE

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

raw\_training\_df

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ├─────────────── 80% ───────────────┐

&#x20;    │                                  │

&#x20;    ▼                                  ▼

&#x20;TRAIN                              TEMP

&#x20;    │                                  │

&#x20;    │                         ┌────────┴────────┐

&#x20;    │                         │                 │

&#x20;    │                        10%               10%

&#x20;    │                         │                 │

&#x20;    ▼                         ▼                 ▼

DataProcessor.fit()         VAL               TEST

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ├── transform VAL

&#x20;    └── transform TEST

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

FeatureEngineer.fit() on TRAIN

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ├── transform VAL

&#x20;    └── transform TEST

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ▼

ServiceModel.train(

&#x20;   TRAIN,

&#x20;   VAL,

&#x20;   TEST

)

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ├── Comment TF-IDF fit TRAIN only

&#x20;    ├── SVD fit TRAIN only

&#x20;    ├── Comment transform VAL

&#x20;    ├── Comment transform TEST

&#x20;    │

&#x20;    ├── Models fit TRAIN

&#x20;    ├── Models evaluated VAL

&#x20;    ├── Best model selected

&#x20;    └── Best model evaluated TEST



That is the structure I would keep.



One further correction: the revised model.py above uses a separate status\_preprocess object. That object is saved inside service\_model.pkl, so your prediction code can correctly calculate hotel reservation\_status probabilities without trying to reference undefined variables such as status\_model, X\_all\_transformed, or df.



Also, your app.py currently performs batch prediction itself, rather than calling ServiceModel.predict() row-by-row. That is good for the 150k+ row performance problem you were addressing. The model.py predict() method should therefore remain mainly for individual/UI prediction, while initialize\_prediction() handles the fast batch operation.

&#x20;   if scores.ndim == 1:

&#x20;   scores = (

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   exp\_scores = np.exp(

&#x20;           keepdims=True

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

\# RISK CALCULATION

\# =====================================================



import numpy as np



class\_order = list(

&#x20;   clf.classes\_

)



risk\_weights = {

&#x20;   1: 1.0,

&#x20;   2: 0.7,

&#x20;   3: 0.3,

&#x20;   4: 0.1,

&#x20;   5: 0.0

}



sla\_risk = np.zeros(

&#x20;   len(pred\_ratings),

&#x20;   dtype=float

)



for i, cls in enumerate(

&#x20;   class\_order

):



&#x20;   if i >= probs.shape\[1]:

&#x20;   sla\_risk += (

&#x20;       probs\[:, i] \*

&#x20;       risk\_weights.get(

&#x20;           cls,

&#x20;           0

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



sla\_risk\_score = (

&#x20;   sla\_risk \* 100

)



\# =====================================================

\# =====================================================

&#x20;   5: 10,

&#x20;   4: 25,

&#x20;   3: 50,

&#x20;   \[

&#x20;       rating\_map.get(

&#x20;           50

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       for rating in pred\_ratings

&#x20;   ],

&#x20;   dtype=float

)



risk\_score = (

&#x20;   0.6 \* base\_risk +

&#x20;   0.4 \* sla\_risk\_score

)



\# =====================================================

\# ADD PREDICTIONS

\# =====================================================



prediction\_df\[

&#x20;   "predicted\_rating"

] = pred\_ratings



prediction\_df\[

&#x20;   "sla\_risk\_score"

] = np.round(

&#x20;   sla\_risk\_score,

&#x20;   1

)



prediction\_df\[

&#x20;   "risk\_score"

] = np.round(

&#x20;   risk\_score,

&#x20;   1

)



\# -----------------------------------------------------

\#

\# Do NOT call \_generate\_comment() 150,000 times.

&#x20;                   n\_estimators=300,

&#x20;                   learning\_rate=0.05,

&#x20;                   num\_leaves=31,

&#x20;                   class\_weight=class\_weight\_dict,

&#x20;                   random\_state=42,

&#x20;                   verbosity=-1

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           )



&#x20;       ])



&#x20;   }



self.models = models



\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # EVALUATION HELPER

&#x20;   # =========================================================



&#x20;   def evaluate(

&#x20;       model,

&#x20;       X\_eval,

&#x20;       y\_true,

&#x20;       name,

&#x20;       show\_report=True

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       preds = model.predict(

&#x20;           X\_eval

&#x20;       )



f1 = f1\_score(

&#x20;           y\_true,

&#x20;           preds,

&#x20;           average="weighted"

&#x20;       )



try:



&#x20;           clf = model.named\_steps\[

&#x20;               "clf"

&#x20;           ]



if hasattr(

&#x20;               clf,

&#x20;               "predict\_proba"

&#x20;           ):



&#x20;               probs = model.predict\_proba(

&#x20;                   X\_eval

&#x20;               )



&#x20;           else:



&#x20;               scores = model.decision\_function(

&#x20;                   X\_eval

&#x20;               )



&#x20;               scores = np.asarray(

&#x20;                   scores

&#x20;               )



if scores.ndim == 1:



&#x20;                   scores = np.column\_stack(

&#x20;                       \[

&#x20;                           -scores,

&#x20;                           scores

&#x20;                       ]

&#x20;                   )



exp = np.exp(

&#x20;                   scores -

&#x20;                   np.max(

&#x20;                       scores,

&#x20;                       axis=1,

&#x20;                       keepdims=True

&#x20;                   )

&#x20;               )



probs = (

&#x20;                   exp /

&#x20;                   exp.sum(

&#x20;                       axis=1,

&#x20;                       keepdims=True

&#x20;                   )

&#x20;               )



roc = roc\_auc\_score(

&#x20;               y\_true,

&#x20;               probs,

&#x20;               multi\_class="ovr",

&#x20;               average="weighted"

&#x20;           )



except Exception as e:



&#x20;           print(

&#x20;               f"\[WARNING] ROC-AUC failed "

&#x20;               f"for {name}: {e}"

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           roc = 0.0



if show\_report:



&#x20;           print()

&#x20;           print("==============================")

&#x20;           print(name)

&#x20;           print("==============================")



print(

&#x20;               classification\_report(

&#x20;                   y\_true,

&#x20;                   preds

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           )



print(

&#x20;               "F1 Score :",

&#x20;               round(

&#x20;                   f1,

&#x20;                   4

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           )



print(

&#x20;               "ROC-AUC  :",

&#x20;               round(

&#x20;                   roc,

&#x20;                   4

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           )



return {



&#x20;           "model": name,

&#x20;           "f1": f1,

&#x20;           "roc": roc



&#x20;       }



\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # TRAIN MODELS

&#x20;   # =========================================================



&#x20;   print()

&#x20;   print("==============================")

&#x20;   print("TRAINING MODELS")

&#x20;   print("==============================")



for name, model in models.items():



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           f"Training {name}..."

&#x20;       )



model.fit(

&#x20;           X\_train,

&#x20;           y\_train

&#x20;       )



print(

&#x20;           f"{name} completed."

&#x20;       )



\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # RESERVATION STATUS MODEL

&#x20;   # =========================================================



&#x20;   print()

&#x20;   print("==============================")

&#x20;   print("RESERVATION STATUS TRAINING")

&#x20;   print("==============================")



status\_preprocess = ColumnTransformer(\[



&#x20;       (

&#x20;           "text",

&#x20;           ),

&#x20;           structured\_features\_with\_comments

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   ])



print(

&#x20;       "Fitting reservation status preprocessing..."

&#x20;   )



X\_train\_status = (

&#x20;       status\_preprocess.fit\_transform(

&#x20;           X\_train

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



X\_val\_status = (

&#x20;       status\_preprocess.transform(

&#x20;           X\_val

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



X\_test\_status = (

&#x20;       status\_preprocess.transform(

&#x20;           X\_test

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



self.status\_model = LogisticRegression(

&#x20;       solver="saga",

&#x20;       max\_iter=100,

&#x20;       tol=1e-2,

&#x20;       class\_weight="balanced",

&#x20;       n\_jobs=-1

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       "Training Reservation Status Model..."

&#x20;   )



self.status\_model.fit(

&#x20;       X\_train\_status,

&#x20;       y\_status\_train

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       "Reservation Status Model completed."

&#x20;   )



self.status\_preprocess = (

&#x20;       status\_preprocess

&#x20;   )



\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # RESERVATION STATUS EVALUATION

&#x20;   # =========================================================



&#x20;   print()

&#x20;   print("==============================")

&#x20;   print("RESERVATION STATUS EVALUATION")

&#x20;   print("==============================")



status\_preds = (

&#x20;       self.status\_model.predict(

&#x20;           X\_test\_status

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       classification\_report(

&#x20;   )



\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # VALIDATION

&#x20;   print("VALIDATION")

&#x20;   print("==============================")



validation\_results = \[]



for name, model in models.items():



&#x20;       result = evaluate(

validation\_results.append(

\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # SELECT BEST MODEL

validation\_df\["final\_score"] = (

validation\_df = validation\_df.sort\_values(

print()

print(

&#x20;           index=False

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # BEST MODEL

&#x20;   self.best\_model\_name = (

&#x20;       validation\_df.iloc\[0]\["model"]

&#x20;   )



self.best\_model = (

&#x20;       self.models\[

&#x20;           self.best\_model\_name

&#x20;       ]

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       "\\nBEST MODEL SELECTED:",

&#x20;       self.best\_model\_name

&#x20;   )



\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # FINAL TEST EVALUATION

&#x20;   # =========================================================



&#x20;   print()

&#x20;   print("==============================")

&#x20;   print("FINAL TEST EVALUATION")

&#x20;   print("==============================")



test\_result = evaluate(

&#x20;   )



self.results\_df = pd.DataFrame(\[



&#x20;       {



&#x20;           "model":

&#x20;               self.best\_model\_name,



&#x20;           "f1":

&#x20;               test\_result\["f1"],



&#x20;           "roc":

&#x20;       }



&#x20;   ])



\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # REFERENCE DATA

&#x20;   # =========================================================



&#x20;   self.df\_reference = pd.concat(

\# =========================================================

fields = \[

joblib.dump(

&#x20;   metadata\_path = self.config.get(

import json

if os.path.exists(

metadata.update({

with open(

print(

&#x20;   )
