def set\_model(

&#x20;   self,

&#x20;   name: str

):



&#x20;   if name in self.models:



&#x20;       self.best\_model\_name = name



&#x20;       self.best\_model = (

&#x20;           self.models\[name]

&#x20;       )



\# =====================================================

\# PREDICT

\# =====================================================



def predict(

&#x20;   self,

&#x20;   x: dict

):



&#x20;   structured\_features = \[



&#x20;       "comment",

&#x20;       "hotel",

&#x20;       "meal",

&#x20;       "market\_segment",

&#x20;       "distribution\_channel",

&#x20;       "deposit\_type",

&#x20;       "customer\_type",

&#x20;       "season\_group",

&#x20;       "country\_group",

&#x20;       "adr\_group",

&#x20;       "previous\_cancellations\_group",

&#x20;       "days\_in\_waiting\_list\_group",

&#x20;       "guest\_group",

&#x20;       "client\_segment",

&#x20;       "is\_top\_bad\_client",

&#x20;       "client\_bad\_rate"



&#x20;   ]



input\_df = pd.DataFrame(

&#x20;       \[x]

&#x20;   )



for col in structured\_features:



&#x20;       if col not in input\_df.columns:



&#x20;           input\_df\[col] = "unknown"



input\_df\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       input\_df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;   )



X\_input = input\_df\[

&#x20;       structured\_features

&#x20;   ]



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # RATING PREDICTION

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   pred\_rating = int(

&#x20;       self.best\_model.predict(

&#x20;           X\_input

&#x20;       )\[0]

&#x20;   )



clf = (

&#x20;       self.best\_model

&#x20;       .named\_steps\["clf"]

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # RESERVATION STATUS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   X\_status = (

&#x20;       self.status\_preprocess.transform(

&#x20;           X\_input

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



status\_probs = (

&#x20;       self.status\_model.predict\_proba(

&#x20;           X\_status

&#x20;       )\[0]

&#x20;   )



status\_class\_order = (

&#x20;       self.status\_model.classes\_

&#x20;   )



prob\_canceled = 0.0

&#x20;   prob\_check\_out = 0.0

&#x20;   prob\_no\_show = 0.0



for i, cls in enumerate(

&#x20;       status\_class\_order

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       probability = (

&#x20;           status\_probs\[i] \*

&#x20;           100

&#x20;       )



if cls == "canceled":



&#x20;           prob\_canceled = round(

&#x20;               probability,

&#x20;               1

&#x20;           )



elif cls == "check-out":



&#x20;           prob\_check\_out = round(

&#x20;               probability,

&#x20;               1

&#x20;           )



elif cls == "no-show":



&#x20;           prob\_no\_show = round(

&#x20;               probability,

&#x20;               1

&#x20;           )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # RATING PROBABILITY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   if hasattr(

&#x20;       clf,

&#x20;       "predict\_proba"

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       probs = (

&#x20;           self.best\_model

&#x20;           .predict\_proba(

&#x20;               X\_input

&#x20;           )\[0]

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   else:



&#x20;       scores = (

&#x20;           self.best\_model

&#x20;           .decision\_function(

&#x20;               X\_input

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



scores = np.asarray(

&#x20;           scores

&#x20;       )



if scores.ndim == 2:



&#x20;           scores = scores\[0]



exp = np.exp(

&#x20;           scores -

&#x20;           np.max(scores)

&#x20;       )



probs = (

&#x20;           exp /

&#x20;           np.sum(exp)

&#x20;       )



class\_order = list(

&#x20;       clf.classes\_

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # SLA RISK

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   risk\_weights = {



&#x20;       1: 1.0,

&#x20;       2: 0.7,

&#x20;       3: 0.3,

&#x20;       4: 0.1,

&#x20;       5: 0.0



&#x20;   }



sla\_risk = 0.0



for i, cls in enumerate(

&#x20;       class\_order

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       if i >= len(probs):

&#x20;           continue



sla\_risk += (



&#x20;           probs\[i] \*

&#x20;           risk\_weights.get(

&#x20;               cls,

&#x20;               0

&#x20;           )



&#x20;       )



sla\_risk\_score = round(

&#x20;       sla\_risk \* 100,

&#x20;       1

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # BASE RISK

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   rating\_map = {



&#x20;       5: 10,

&#x20;       4: 25,

&#x20;       3: 50,

&#x20;       2: 75,

&#x20;       1: 90



&#x20;   }



base\_risk = rating\_map.get(

&#x20;       pred\_rating,

&#x20;       50

&#x20;   )



risk\_score = round(



&#x20;       0.6 \*

&#x20;       base\_risk



&#x20;       +



&#x20;       0.4 \*

&#x20;       sla\_risk\_score,



&#x20;       1



&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # COMMENT

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   generated\_comment = (

&#x20;       self.\_generate\_comment(

&#x20;           pred\_rating,

&#x20;           sla\_risk\_score,

&#x20;           risk\_score,

&#x20;           x

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



return (



&#x20;       pred\_rating,



&#x20;       prob\_canceled,



&#x20;       prob\_check\_out,



&#x20;       prob\_no\_show,



&#x20;       sla\_risk\_score,



&#x20;       risk\_score,



&#x20;       generated\_comment



&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

\# COMMENT GENERATION

\# =====================================================



def \_generate\_comment(

&#x20;   self,

&#x20;   rating,

&#x20;   sla\_risk,

&#x20;   risk,

&#x20;   x

):



&#x20;   msg = \[]



if rating == 5:



&#x20;       msg.append(

&#x20;           "Excellent service."

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   elif rating == 4:



&#x20;       msg.append(

&#x20;           "Positive service."

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   elif rating == 3:



&#x20;       msg.append(

&#x20;           "Average service."

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   elif rating == 2:



&#x20;       msg.append(

&#x20;           "Service quality issue."

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   else:



&#x20;       msg.append(

&#x20;           "High dissatisfaction."

&#x20;       )



context\_comments = (

&#x20;       self.\_get\_top\_comments\_dynamic(

&#x20;           rating,

&#x20;           x,

&#x20;           top\_k=20

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



if context\_comments:



&#x20;       ai\_summary = (

&#x20;           self.\_generate\_ai\_summary(

&#x20;               context\_comments,

&#x20;               rating

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



if ai\_summary:



&#x20;           msg.append(

&#x20;               ai\_summary

&#x20;           )



example\_block = \[

&#x20;           "Examples of similar feedback:"

&#x20;       ]



example\_block.extend(



&#x20;           \[

&#x20;               f"{i}. {c}"



&#x20;               for i, c in enumerate(

&#x20;                   context\_comments\[:5],

&#x20;                   1

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           ]



&#x20;       )



msg.append(

&#x20;           "\\n".join(

&#x20;               example\_block

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



else:



&#x20;       msg.append(

&#x20;           "No historical patterns found; "

&#x20;           "using operational signals."

&#x20;       )



return "\\n\\n".join(

&#x20;       msg

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

\# TOP COMMENTS

\# =====================================================



def \_get\_top\_comments\_dynamic(

&#x20;   self,

&#x20;   rating,

&#x20;   x,

&#x20;   top\_k=5

):



&#x20;   df = self.comment\_df.copy()

def \_fit\_bad\_clientdriver(self, df):



&#x20;   df = df.copy()



df\["is\_bad\_rating"] = (

&#x20;       .isin(\[0, 1, 2])

&#x20;   )



\# -------------------------

&#x20;   self.client\_bad\_stats = (

top\_10\_bad\_clients = (

self.top\_bad\_clients = (

&#x20;   )

def \_top\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   from collections import defaultdict



&#x20;   df = df.copy()



&#x20;   df\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   # =====================================================

&#x20;   # RATING LEVEL

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   rating\_db = (

&#x20;       df.groupby(

&#x20;           "final\_rating",

&#x20;       )\["comment"]

&#x20;       .value\_counts()

&#x20;       .groupby(level=0)

&#x20;       .head(10)

&#x20;       .groupby(level=0)

&#x20;       .apply(

&#x20;           lambda x: x.index.get\_level\_values(1).tolist()

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       .to\_dict()

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   # =====================================================

&#x20;   # CLIENT LEVEL

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   client\_db = (

&#x20;       df.groupby(

&#x20;           "client\_email",

&#x20;           dropna=True

&#x20;       )\["comment"]

&#x20;       .value\_counts()

&#x20;       .groupby(level=0)

&#x20;       .head(10)

&#x20;       .groupby(level=0)

&#x20;       .apply(

&#x20;           lambda x: x.index.get\_level\_values(1).tolist()

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       .to\_dict()

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   # =====================================================

&#x20;   # STORE

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df.attrs\["top\_comments\_rating"] = rating\_db

&#x20;   df.attrs\["top\_comments\_client"] = client\_db



&#x20;   print(

&#x20;       "Pre-process - Step 5.5 Top Comments Memory Built"

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   return df



\# =========================================================

\# Step 5.6 Top Comment Clustering - FIT

\# =========================================================



def \_fit\_top20\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   import re

&#x20;   import numpy as np



&#x20;   from sentence\_transformers import SentenceTransformer

&#x20;   from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 FIT Comment Clustering"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 1. ONLY BAD REVIEWS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\_bad = df\[

&#x20;       df\["final\_rating"].isin(\[0, 1, 2])

&#x20;   ].copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 2. CLEAN COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\_bad\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;       .str.lower()

&#x20;   )



def clean\_text(text):



&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'ðÿ\\S\*', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\[^a-z0-9\\s]', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text)



&#x20;       return text.strip()



df\_bad\["comment\_clean"] = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment"]

&#x20;       .apply(clean\_text)

&#x20;   )



\# Remove empty comments

&#x20;   df\_bad = df\_bad\[

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment\_clean"].str.len() > 0

&#x20;   ].copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 3. COUNT COMMENT FREQUENCY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   comment\_counts = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment\_clean"]

&#x20;       .value\_counts()

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 4. TOP 20 COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   top20\_comments = (

&#x20;       comment\_counts

&#x20;       .head(20)

&#x20;   )



if top20\_comments.empty:



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           "Step 5.6 - No valid bad-review comments found"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model = None

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_samples = {}

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_labels = {}

&#x20;       self.top20\_comments = \[]



&#x20;       return



self.top20\_comments = (

&#x20;       top20\_comments.index.tolist()

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Top "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.top20\_comments)} comments selected"

&#x20;   )



for i, comment in enumerate(

&#x20;       self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;       start=1

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           f"  {i:02d}. "

&#x20;           f"{comment} "

&#x20;           f"(count={top20\_comments\[comment]})"

&#x20;       )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 5. SENTENCE TRANSFORMER

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   print(

&#x20;       "Step 5.6 - Loading SentenceTransformer..."

&#x20;   )



self.comment\_embedding\_model = (

&#x20;       SentenceTransformer(

&#x20;           "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 6. EMBED TOP 20 COMMENTS ONLY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   embeddings = (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model.encode(

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           convert\_to\_numpy=True,

&#x20;           normalize\_embeddings=True,

&#x20;           batch\_size=20,

&#x20;           show\_progress\_bar=False

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Generated embeddings for "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.top20\_comments)} comments"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 7. CREATE 10 CLUSTERS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   n\_clusters = min(

&#x20;       10,

&#x20;       len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;   )



if n\_clusters == 1:



&#x20;       clusters = np.zeros(

&#x20;           len(self.top20\_comments),

&#x20;           dtype=int

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   else:



&#x20;       cluster\_model = (

&#x20;           AgglomerativeClustering(

&#x20;               n\_clusters=n\_clusters,

&#x20;               metric="cosine",

&#x20;               linkage="average"

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       clusters = (

&#x20;           cluster\_model.fit\_predict(

&#x20;               embeddings

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 8. STORE CLUSTER LABELS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   self.comment\_cluster\_labels = dict(

&#x20;       zip(

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           clusters

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 9. STORE CLUSTER CENTROIDS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}



self.comment\_cluster\_samples = {}



for cluster\_id in sorted(

&#x20;       set(clusters)

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       cluster\_mask = (

&#x20;           clusters == cluster\_id

&#x20;       )



cluster\_embeddings = (

&#x20;           embeddings\[

&#x20;               cluster\_mask

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;       )



\# Mean embedding

&#x20;       centroid = (

&#x20;           cluster\_embeddings

&#x20;           .mean(axis=0)

&#x20;       )



\# Normalize centroid

&#x20;       centroid\_norm = np.linalg.norm(

&#x20;           centroid

&#x20;       )



if centroid\_norm > 0:



&#x20;           centroid = (

&#x20;               centroid /

&#x20;               centroid\_norm

&#x20;           )



self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;           cluster\_id

&#x20;       ] = centroid



\# ---------------------------------------------

&#x20;       # Store sample comments

&#x20;       # ---------------------------------------------



&#x20;       cluster\_comments = \[

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments\[i]

&#x20;           for i in range(

&#x20;               len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;           )

&#x20;           if clusters\[i] == cluster\_id

&#x20;       ]



self.comment\_cluster\_samples\[

&#x20;           cluster\_id

&#x20;       ] = cluster\_comments\[:3]



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - "

&#x20;       "Step 5.6 FIT Top Comment Clustering completed"

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.comment\_cluster\_centroids)} clusters created"

&#x20;   )



\# =========================================================

\# Step 5.6 Top Comment Clustering - APPLY

\# =========================================================



def \_apply\_top20\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   import re

&#x20;   import numpy as np



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 APPLY Comment Clustering"

&#x20;   )



df = df.copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 1. CLEAN COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;       .str.lower()

&#x20;   )



def clean\_text(text):



&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'ðÿ\\S\*', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\[^a-z0-9\\s]', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text)



&#x20;       return text.strip()



df\["comment\_clean"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .apply(clean\_text)

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 2. CHECK WHETHER MODEL EXISTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   if (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model is None

&#x20;       or not self.comment\_cluster\_centroids

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       df\["cluster"] = -1



&#x20;       df\["business\_categories"] = (

&#x20;           "Other / Acceptable Service"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       df\["sample\_comments"] = None



&#x20;       return df



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 3. UNIQUE NON-EMPTY COMMENTS ONLY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   unique\_comments = (

&#x20;       df.loc\[

&#x20;           df\["comment\_clean"].str.len() > 0,

&#x20;           "comment\_clean"

&#x20;       ]

&#x20;       .drop\_duplicates()

&#x20;       .tolist()

&#x20;   )



if not unique\_comments:



&#x20;       df\["cluster"] = -1



&#x20;       df\["business\_categories"] = (

&#x20;           "Other / Acceptable Service"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       df\["sample\_comments"] = None



&#x20;       return df



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Applying clustering to "

&#x20;       f"{len(unique\_comments):,} unique comments "

&#x20;       f"from {len(df):,} rows"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 4. EMBED UNIQUE COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   embeddings = (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model.encode(

&#x20;           unique\_comments,

&#x20;           convert\_to\_numpy=True,

&#x20;           normalize\_embeddings=True,

&#x20;           batch\_size=64,

&#x20;           show\_progress\_bar=False

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 5. BUILD CENTROID MATRIX

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   cluster\_ids = list(

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_centroids.keys()

&#x20;   )



centroid\_matrix = np.vstack(

&#x20;       \[

&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;               cluster\_id

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;           for cluster\_id in cluster\_ids

&#x20;       ]

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 6. COSINE SIMILARITY

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # Both embeddings and centroids are normalized.

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # Therefore:

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # cosine similarity

&#x20;   # =

&#x20;   # dot product

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   similarity\_matrix = (

&#x20;       embeddings @ centroid\_matrix.T

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 7. FIND BEST CLUSTER

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   best\_cluster\_indices = (

&#x20;       np.argmax(

&#x20;           similarity\_matrix,

&#x20;           axis=1

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



unique\_cluster\_labels = \[

&#x20;       cluster\_ids\[index]

&#x20;       for index in best\_cluster\_indices

&#x20;   ]



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 8. COMMENT -> CLUSTER LOOKUP

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   comment\_to\_cluster = dict(

&#x20;       zip(

&#x20;           unique\_comments,

&#x20;           unique\_cluster\_labels

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



df\["cluster"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment\_clean"]

&#x20;       .map(

&#x20;           comment\_to\_cluster

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       .fillna(-1)

&#x20;       .astype(int)

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 9. BUSINESS CATEGORIES

&#x20;   # =====================================================

Yes. With the preprocess.py you just provided, the architecture is clear.



Your intended distinction is:



rating = raw/original rating from the database. It can contain missing values.



rating\_predicted = rating predicted from the comment when raw rating is missing.



final\_rating = the final rating used by downstream ML. It is rating where available, otherwise rating\_predicted.



The IterativeImputer does not impute rating or final\_rating because both are explicitly excluded.



So final\_rating is the correct target for FeatureEngineer and ServiceModel.



Your current flow



RAW DATABASE

│

├── rating

│     ├── available

│     │      ↓

│     │   use original rating

│     │

│     └── missing

│            ↓

│       rating\_model

│            ↓

│       rating\_predicted

│

▼

final\_rating

│

│   rating.fillna(rating\_predicted)

│

▼

FeatureEngineer

│

├── season\_group

├── country\_group

├── adr\_group

├── previous\_cancellations\_group

├── days\_in\_waiting\_list\_group

├── guest\_group

├── client\_segment

├── client\_bad\_rate

├── is\_top\_bad\_client

└── comment clustering

│

▼

ServiceModel

│

├── Target = final\_rating

├── Reservation status model

├── Rating model comparison

├── Best model

├── SLA risk

└── Comment generation



Therefore, don't change these



In feature\_engineering.py:



df\["final\_rating"]



is correct.



For example:



df\["is\_bad\_rating"] = (

&#x20;   df\["final\_rating"]

&#x20;   .isin(\[0, 1, 2])

&#x20;   .astype(int)

)



Correct.



And:



df.groupby("final\_rating")



Correct.



And:



df\_bad = df\[

&#x20;   df\["final\_rating"].isin(\[0, 1, 2])

].copy()



Correct.



In model.py:



y\_train = train\_df\["final\_rating"]

y\_val = val\_df\["final\_rating"]

y\_test = test\_df\["final\_rating"]



is also correct.



One important issue I see



There is a subtle issue in your preprocess.py.



You correctly exclude:



"rating",

"final\_rating",

"rating\_predicted"



from the IterativeImputer:



df2 = df.drop(

&#x20;   columns=\[

&#x20;       "rating",

&#x20;       "final\_rating",

&#x20;       "rating\_predicted"

&#x20;   ],

&#x20;   errors="ignore"

).copy()



But after that, \_impute() reconstructs the dataframe with:



result\["rating"] = df\["rating"]

result\["final\_rating"] = df\["final\_rating"]



This means final\_rating is preserved exactly as intended.



So the statement:



final\_rating is the rating that has gone through the imputation process



needs a small correction.



Technically, based on this code, final\_rating does not go through IterativeImputer.



Instead:



rating

&#x20; │

&#x20; ├── not missing ──────────────┐

&#x20; │                             │

&#x20; └── missing                   │

&#x20;      ↓                        │

&#x20; rating\_model                  │

&#x20;      ↓                        │

&#x20; rating\_predicted              │

&#x20;      │                        │

&#x20;      └────────┬───────────────┘

&#x20;               ↓

&#x20;        final\_rating



So final\_rating is your business-level imputed/filled rating, rather than an IterativeImputer output.



That distinction is actually good for your ML design because you don't want the numerical rating target being altered by an unsupervised IterativeImputer.



One other thing



Your rating\_model itself is trained only on:



X = train\["comment"].fillna("")

y = train\["rating"].astype(int)



So missing ratings are inferred from comments, which is a sensible approach for your hotel review dataset.



Bottom line



Your three files should follow this contract:



Stage

Column

Purpose

Raw DB

rating

Original hotel rating

Preprocess

rating\_predicted

Predicted only when rating is missing

Preprocess

final\_rating

Final target used downstream

Feature Engineering

final\_rating

Behaviour/rating features

Service Model

final\_rating

Classification target

Service Model

reservation\_status

Separate classification target



So I would leave the final\_rating references in both model.py and feature\_engineering.py exactly as they are.



There is no reason to replace them with rating.



The next useful step is to check your app.py training flow, because your ServiceModel.train() currently expects three arguments:



train(

&#x20;   train\_df,

&#x20;   val\_df,

&#x20;   test\_df

)



while your earlier application flow may have been calling service\_model.train(df) with only one dataframe. That would be a more important integration issue to resolve than the rating/final\_rating naming.

final\_rating created

Correct conceptual flow



Because you want final\_rating to be the authoritative rating after missing ratings are predicted, the pipeline should conceptually be:



RAW DATA

&#x20;  │     └── missing rating

&#x20;  │

&#x20;  ▼

&#x20;  │

&#x20;  │

rating

&#x20; ↓

used by DataProcessor to determine missing values



final\_rating

used by FeatureEngineer for business analysis

df\["final\_rating"].isin(\[0, 1, 2])



df.groupby("final\_rating")



df\["final\_rating"].notna()

\_fit\_clientdriver\_behaviour()



because:



df.groupby("client\_email")\["final\_rating"].mean()



should calculate the client's average based on the final rating, including ratings predicted from comments.

and:

should identify bad reviews using:



df\["final\_rating"].isin(\[0, 1, 2])

inside FeatureEngineer.

Yes. This is a different issue from stratify. Removing stratify was correct, but now the error is coming from your DataProcessor.\_impute().



The key error is:



ValueError: y contains previously unseen labels: '16732'



What is happening



You fit the LabelEncoder only on the training data:



le.fit\_transform(df2\[col].astype(str))



Then, when transforming validation data, this happens:



le.transform(

&#x20;   df2\[col].astype(str)

)



The validation set contains a value such as:



16732



that did not occur in the training set.



LabelEncoder cannot handle unseen categories, so it crashes.



Recommended fix



Since you want to keep your existing architecture, do not change your train/validation/test splitting again.



Instead, modify only \_impute() in preprocess.py.



Replace this part:



\# Encode categorical columns used by imputer

for col, le in self.imputer\_encoders.items():



&#x20;   df2\[col] = (

&#x20;       le.transform(

&#x20;           df2\[col].astype(str)

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



with:



\# Encode categorical columns used by imputer

\# Handle values that were not seen during training.

for col, le in self.imputer\_encoders.items():



&#x20;   mapping = {

&#x20;       value: index

&#x20;       for index, value in enumerate(

&#x20;           le.classes\_

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   df2\[col] = (

&#x20;       df2\[col]

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;       .map(mapping)

&#x20;       .fillna(-1)

&#x20;       .astype(int)

&#x20;   )



This prevents:



ValueError: y contains previously unseen labels



because an unseen validation/test value is converted to:



\-1



instead of causing LabelEncoder.transform() to fail.

Your current code later does this:

&#x20;   .astype(int)

Use:



Primary:

Why?



Macro F1 calculates:



(F1\_0 + F1\_1 + F1\_2 + F1\_3 + F1\_4 + F1\_5 + F1\_6) / 7



so every rating receives equal importance.



That is much more appropriate when you care about identifying bad reviews.

Yes. The key change is:



final\_rating must be created before train\_test\_split(), because it is your target, while the normal IterativeImputer must remain completely separate and must never impute final\_rating.



Your current DataProcessor.fit() cannot do this correctly if you split the raw data first, because the rating model only sees the training subset.



The clean flow should be:



RAW DATABASE

&#x20;    ↓

DataProcessor: clean rating/comment

&#x20;    ↓

Fit rating model using available rating

&#x20;    ↓

Predict missing rating

&#x20;    ↓

Create final\_rating

&#x20;    ↓

SPLIT using final\_rating

&#x20;    ↓

Train / Validation / Test

&#x20;    ↓

Normal IterativeImputer

&#x20;    ↓

Feature Engineering

&#x20;    ↓

Service Model



However, there is an important leakage consideration: if you fit the rating model using the entire dataset before splitting, the target-generation model has seen comments from validation/test. If final\_rating is intended as the completed target label, this may be acceptable for your assignment's preprocessing definition, but it is not a strictly leakage-free evaluation.



Below is the amended preprocess.py structure that separates the two imputation processes.



Replace your DataProcessor with this version

&#x20;   def \_fit\_encoders(self, df):

&#x20;       for col in cols:

&#x20;               .fillna("missing")

&#x20;       if len(train) == 0:

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       valid = y.between(

&#x20;           0,

&#x20;           6

&#x20;       y = y.loc\[valid]



&#x20;       if y.nunique() < 2:

&#x20;           ),



&#x20;           (

&#x20;               "clf",

&#x20;               LogisticRegression(

&#x20;                   max\_iter=1000,

&#x20;                   class\_weight="balanced"

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       ])



self.rating\_model.fit(

df.loc\[

&#x20;       # If no rating model exists

Yes — this error is because your training data has final\_rating created before the split, but your fresh dashboard database does not contain final\_rating.



Your \_impute() currently assumes this always exists:

That is not valid for a raw dashboard DB.



The correct design



You want:



Raw DB has rating = original rating, including missing values.



rating\_model predicts missing rating.



final\_rating = original rating + predicted rating.



final\_rating is used as the ML target.



The normal IterativeImputer must never touch rating, final\_rating, or rating\_predicted.



Dashboard/raw prediction data can create final\_rating during processor.transform().



Therefore \_impute() must safely handle cases where final\_rating doesn't yet exist.



The immediate fix is to change the final part of \_impute().

With this

&#x20;                   ▼

&#x20;            normal DataProcessor

&#x20;                   │

&#x20;                   ▼

&#x20;            IterativeImputer

&#x20;                   │

&#x20;         DOES NOT TOUCH:

&#x20;         • rating

&#x20;         • final\_rating

&#x20;         • rating\_predicted



One caveat: because prepare\_final\_rating() trains the comment-rating model on the entire dataset before the split, the validation/test final\_rating labels are partly generated by a model that has seen their comments. That is appropriate if your goal is specifically to create a completed target from missing ratings, but it does introduce target-generation leakage if you're evaluating the downstream model as though final\_rating were a fully independent ground-truth label.

It is not actually running the SentenceTransformer twice in the log you showed.



What is happening is that FeatureEngineer Step 5.6 is being applied twice to the training data.



You can see it here:



Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 FIT Top Comment Clustering completed

Step 5.6 - 10 clusters created



Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 APPLY Comment Clustering

Step 5.6 - Applying clustering to 12,052 unique comments from 94,556 rows

Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 APPLY Top Comment Clustering completed

FeatureEngineering fitted



Then immediately:



Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 APPLY Comment Clustering

Step 5.6 - Applying clustering to 12,052 unique comments from 94,556 rows

Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 APPLY Top Comment Clustering completed

FeatureEngineering transform completed



Why?



Because your FeatureEngineer.fit\_transform() is almost certainly doing something equivalent to:



def fit\_transform(self, train\_df):



&#x20;   self.fit(train\_df)



&#x20;   return self.transform(train\_df)



And inside fit() you are already applying the clustering after fitting it.



So the sequence becomes:



feature\_engineer.fit(train\_df)

&#x20;   │

&#x20;   ├── FIT clustering

&#x20;   │

&#x20;   └── APPLY clustering       ← FIRST TIME

&#x20;   │

&#x20;   ▼

feature\_engineer.transform(train\_df)

&#x20;   │

&#x20;   └── APPLY clustering       ← SECOND TIME



That's exactly what your log demonstrates.



The better fix



Since you want:



FIT

&#x20; ↓

learn clustering model

&#x20; ↓

save clustering model



TRANSFORM

&#x20; ↓

apply already-fitted clustering



your FeatureEngineer.fit() should fit the clustering model but not apply it to the training dataframe.



Then fit\_transform() can safely do:



def fit\_transform(self, train\_df):



&#x20;   self.fit(train\_df)



&#x20;   return self.transform(train\_df)



The resulting flow is:



fit(train\_df)

&#x20;   │

&#x20;   └── FIT Top Comment Clustering

&#x20;            │

&#x20;            └── 10 clusters created

&#x20;            

transform(train\_df)

&#x20;   │

&#x20;   └── APPLY Top Comment Clustering



So Step 5.6 should appear once during fit/transform, not twice.



Your validation and test are already correct



This part:



\[INFO] Transforming validation features...

...

Step 5.6 - Applying clustering to 11 unique comments from 11,820 rows



and:



\[INFO] Transforming test features...

...

Step 5.6 - Applying clustering to 12 unique comments from 11,820 rows



is correct.



The intended behavior is:



TRAIN

&#x20; FIT clustering

&#x20; APPLY clustering once



VALIDATION

&#x20; APPLY existing clustering once



TEST

&#x20; APPLY existing clustering once



So you want this log:

No second 12,052-comment application for training.



One more important point



The line:



Step 5.6 - Generated embeddings for 20 comments



is only the fitting stage. The 12,052 comments are the application stage.



So:



20 comments



≠



12,052 comments



The 20 is likely your selected top/sample comments used to learn the clusters, while the 12,052 are unique comments to which the learned clustering is subsequently applied.

Yes. The slow part is not the clustering itself. Your \_fit\_top20\_comment() is fast because it embeds only 20 comments.



The slow part is \_apply\_top20\_comment():



12,052 unique comments from 118,196 rows



That means you're running SentenceTransformer.encode() on 12,052 different comments every time \_apply\_top20\_comment() is called.



And from your previous log, it is being called during:



FeatureEngineer fit\_transform() on 94,556 training rows



FeatureEngineer transform() on 11,820 validation rows



FeatureEngineer transform() on 11,820 test rows



Later, dashboard processing again



The biggest problem is that the training set is already clustered during fit, then clustered again during transform.



What I recommend



Since your model only needs the top 20 bad-review comments, you don't need to generate SentenceTransformer embeddings for every unique comment.



Use this logic:



During FIT:



Find top 20 bad comments.



Embed those 20.



Create clusters.



Save the cluster centroids.



Build a lookup dictionary for the exact top-20 comments.



During APPLY:



First check whether the cleaned comment is one of the known top-20 comments.



If yes → assign its existing cluster immediately.



Only embed unknown comments that actually need semantic clustering.



Better still, for your dashboard, you can assign only top-20 comments to clusters and set everything else to -1.



This makes the operation dramatically faster.

)



through the embedding section with a top-20 lookup first.



For your use case, I would actually change \_apply\_top20\_comment() so that it does not embed 12,052 comments at all.

def \_fit\_bad\_clientdriver(self, df):



&#x20;   df = df.copy()



df\["is\_bad\_rating"] = (

&#x20;       .isin(\[0, 1, 2])

&#x20;   )



\# -------------------------

&#x20;   # Client bad rate

&#x20;   self.client\_bad\_stats = (

top\_10\_bad\_clients = (

self.top\_bad\_clients = (

&#x20;   )

def \_top\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   from collections import defaultdict



&#x20;   df = df.copy()



&#x20;   df\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   # =====================================================

&#x20;   # RATING LEVEL

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   rating\_db = (

&#x20;       df.groupby(

&#x20;           "final\_rating",

&#x20;       )\["comment"]

&#x20;       .value\_counts()

&#x20;       .groupby(level=0)

&#x20;       .head(10)

&#x20;       .groupby(level=0)

&#x20;       .apply(

&#x20;           lambda x: x.index.get\_level\_values(1).tolist()

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       .to\_dict()

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   # =====================================================

&#x20;   # CLIENT LEVEL

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   client\_db = (

&#x20;       df.groupby(

&#x20;           "client\_email",

&#x20;           dropna=True

&#x20;       )\["comment"]

&#x20;       .value\_counts()

&#x20;       .groupby(level=0)

&#x20;       .head(10)

&#x20;       .groupby(level=0)

&#x20;       .apply(

&#x20;           lambda x: x.index.get\_level\_values(1).tolist()

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       .to\_dict()

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   # =====================================================

&#x20;   # STORE

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df.attrs\["top\_comments\_rating"] = rating\_db

&#x20;   df.attrs\["top\_comments\_client"] = client\_db



&#x20;   print(

&#x20;       "Pre-process - Step 5.5 Top Comments Memory Built"

&#x20;   )



&#x20;   return df



\# =========================================================

\# Step 5.6 Top Comment Clustering - FIT

\# =========================================================



def \_fit\_top20\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   import re

&#x20;   import numpy as np



&#x20;   from sentence\_transformers import SentenceTransformer

&#x20;   from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 FIT Comment Clustering"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 1. ONLY BAD REVIEWS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\_bad = df\[

&#x20;       df\["final\_rating"].isin(\[0, 1, 2])

&#x20;   ].copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 2. CLEAN COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\_bad\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;       .str.lower()

&#x20;   )



def clean\_text(text):



&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'ðÿ\\S\*', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\[^a-z0-9\\s]', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text)



&#x20;       return text.strip()



df\_bad\["comment\_clean"] = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment"]

&#x20;       .apply(clean\_text)

&#x20;   )



\# Remove empty comments

&#x20;   df\_bad = df\_bad\[

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment\_clean"].str.len() > 0

&#x20;   ].copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 3. COUNT COMMENT FREQUENCY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   comment\_counts = (

&#x20;       df\_bad\["comment\_clean"]

&#x20;       .value\_counts()

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 4. TOP 20 COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   top20\_comments = (

&#x20;       comment\_counts

&#x20;       .head(20)

&#x20;   )



if top20\_comments.empty:



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           "Step 5.6 - No valid bad-review comments found"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model = None

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_samples = {}

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_labels = {}

&#x20;       self.top20\_comments = \[]



&#x20;       return



self.top20\_comments = (

&#x20;       top20\_comments.index.tolist()

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Top "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.top20\_comments)} comments selected"

&#x20;   )



for i, comment in enumerate(

&#x20;       self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;       start=1

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           f"  {i:02d}. "

&#x20;           f"{comment} "

&#x20;           f"(count={top20\_comments\[comment]})"

&#x20;       )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 5. SENTENCE TRANSFORMER

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   print(

&#x20;       "Step 5.6 - Loading SentenceTransformer..."

&#x20;   )



self.comment\_embedding\_model = (

&#x20;       SentenceTransformer(

&#x20;           "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 6. EMBED TOP 20 COMMENTS ONLY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   embeddings = (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model.encode(

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           convert\_to\_numpy=True,

&#x20;           normalize\_embeddings=True,

&#x20;           batch\_size=20,

&#x20;           show\_progress\_bar=False

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Generated embeddings for "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.top20\_comments)} comments"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 7. CREATE 10 CLUSTERS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   n\_clusters = min(

&#x20;       10,

&#x20;       len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;   )



if n\_clusters == 1:



&#x20;       clusters = np.zeros(

&#x20;           len(self.top20\_comments),

&#x20;           dtype=int

&#x20;       )



&#x20;   else:



&#x20;       cluster\_model = (

&#x20;           AgglomerativeClustering(

&#x20;               n\_clusters=n\_clusters,

&#x20;               metric="cosine",

&#x20;               linkage="average"

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       clusters = (

&#x20;           cluster\_model.fit\_predict(

&#x20;               embeddings

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 8. STORE CLUSTER LABELS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   self.comment\_cluster\_labels = dict(

&#x20;       zip(

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           clusters

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 9. STORE CLUSTER CENTROIDS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}



self.comment\_cluster\_samples = {}



for cluster\_id in sorted(

&#x20;       set(clusters)

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       cluster\_mask = (

&#x20;           clusters == cluster\_id

&#x20;       )



cluster\_embeddings = (

&#x20;           embeddings\[

&#x20;               cluster\_mask

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;       )



\# Mean embedding

&#x20;       centroid = (

&#x20;           cluster\_embeddings

&#x20;           .mean(axis=0)

&#x20;       )



\# Normalize centroid

&#x20;       centroid\_norm = np.linalg.norm(

&#x20;           centroid

&#x20;       )



if centroid\_norm > 0:



&#x20;           centroid = (

&#x20;               centroid /

&#x20;               centroid\_norm

&#x20;           )



self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;           cluster\_id

&#x20;       ] = centroid



\# ---------------------------------------------

&#x20;       # Store sample comments

&#x20;       # ---------------------------------------------



&#x20;       cluster\_comments = \[

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments\[i]

&#x20;           for i in range(

&#x20;               len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;           )

&#x20;           if clusters\[i] == cluster\_id

&#x20;       ]



self.comment\_cluster\_samples\[

&#x20;           cluster\_id

&#x20;       ] = cluster\_comments\[:3]



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - "

&#x20;       "Step 5.6 FIT Top Comment Clustering completed"

&#x20;   )



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - "

&#x20;       f"{len(self.comment\_cluster\_centroids)} clusters created"

&#x20;   )



\# =========================================================

\# Step 5.6 Top Comment Clustering - APPLY

\# =========================================================



def \_apply\_top20\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;   import re

&#x20;   import numpy as np



print(

&#x20;       "Feature Engineering - Step 5.6 APPLY Comment Clustering"

&#x20;   )



df = df.copy()



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 1. CLEAN COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   df\["comment"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .fillna("")

&#x20;       .astype(str)

&#x20;       .str.lower()

&#x20;   )



def clean\_text(text):



&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'ðÿ\\S\*', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\[^a-z0-9\\s]', ' ', text)

&#x20;       text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text)



&#x20;       return text.strip()



df\["comment\_clean"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment"]

&#x20;       .apply(clean\_text)

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 2. CHECK WHETHER MODEL EXISTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   if (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model is None

&#x20;       or not self.comment\_cluster\_centroids

&#x20;   ):



&#x20;       df\["cluster"] = -1



&#x20;       df\["business\_categories"] = (

&#x20;           "Other / Acceptable Service"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       df\["sample\_comments"] = None



&#x20;       return df



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 3. UNIQUE NON-EMPTY COMMENTS ONLY

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   unique\_comments = (

&#x20;       df.loc\[

&#x20;           df\["comment\_clean"].str.len() > 0,

&#x20;           "comment\_clean"

&#x20;       ]

&#x20;       .drop\_duplicates()

&#x20;       .tolist()

&#x20;   )



if not unique\_comments:



&#x20;       df\["cluster"] = -1



&#x20;       df\["business\_categories"] = (

&#x20;           "Other / Acceptable Service"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       df\["sample\_comments"] = None



&#x20;       return df



print(

&#x20;       f"Step 5.6 - Applying clustering to "

&#x20;       f"{len(unique\_comments):,} unique comments "

&#x20;       f"from {len(df):,} rows"

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 4. EMBED UNIQUE COMMENTS

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   embeddings = (

&#x20;       self.comment\_embedding\_model.encode(

&#x20;           unique\_comments,

&#x20;           convert\_to\_numpy=True,

&#x20;           normalize\_embeddings=True,

&#x20;           batch\_size=64,

&#x20;           show\_progress\_bar=False

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 5. BUILD CENTROID MATRIX

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   cluster\_ids = list(

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_centroids.keys()

&#x20;   )



centroid\_matrix = np.vstack(

&#x20;       \[

&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;               cluster\_id

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;           for cluster\_id in cluster\_ids

&#x20;       ]

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 6. COSINE SIMILARITY

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # Both embeddings and centroids are normalized.

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # Therefore:

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # cosine similarity

&#x20;   # =

&#x20;   # dot product

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   similarity\_matrix = (

&#x20;       embeddings @ centroid\_matrix.T

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 7. FIND BEST CLUSTER

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   best\_cluster\_indices = (

&#x20;       np.argmax(

&#x20;           similarity\_matrix,

&#x20;           axis=1

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



unique\_cluster\_labels = \[

&#x20;       cluster\_ids\[index]

&#x20;       for index in best\_cluster\_indices

&#x20;   ]



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 8. COMMENT -> CLUSTER LOOKUP

&#x20;   # =====================================================



&#x20;   comment\_to\_cluster = dict(

&#x20;       zip(

&#x20;           unique\_comments,

&#x20;           unique\_cluster\_labels

&#x20;       )

&#x20;   )



df\["cluster"] = (

&#x20;       df\["comment\_clean"]

&#x20;       .map(

&#x20;           comment\_to\_cluster

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       .fillna(-1)

&#x20;       .astype(int)

&#x20;   )



\# =====================================================

&#x20;   # 9. BUSINESS CATEGORIES

&#x20;   # =====================================================

Yes. The main reason your 12,052 unique comments step is slow is that \_apply\_top20\_comment() is doing a SentenceTransformer embedding for every unique comment.



There is also a more important issue in your class:



def fit\_transform(self, train\_df):

&#x20;   self.fit(train\_df)

&#x20;   return self.transform(train\_df)



Your fit() already does:



self.\_fit\_top20\_comment(df)

df = self.\_apply\_top20\_comment(df)



Then fit\_transform() calls transform() again, causing the training dataframe's comments to be processed a second time.



I recommend these changes



Do not run transform() a second time inside fit\_transform().



Add a comment → cluster cache.



During APPLY, only SentenceTransformer-encode comments that are not already cached.



Keep your centroid matrix approach — that part is already efficient.



Keep your existing business-category logic.



Avoid changing your model behaviour.

&#x20;       comment\_counts = (

&#x20;       # 4. TOP 20 COMMENTS

&#x20;       top20\_comments = (

&#x20;       if top20\_comments.empty:



&#x20;           print(

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           self.comment\_embedding\_model = None

&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}

&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_labels = {}

&#x20;           return

&#x20;       # 5. SENTENCE TRANSFORMER

&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;       # 7. CREATE 10 CLUSTERS

&#x20;       # =====================================================



&#x20;       n\_clusters = min(

&#x20;           10,

&#x20;           len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;       if n\_clusters == 1:

&#x20;               dtype=int

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           clusters = (

&#x20;               )

&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_labels = dict(

&#x20;               self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           )

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       # =====================================================



&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_centroids = {}



&#x20;       self.comment\_cluster\_samples = {}



&#x20;       for cluster\_id in sorted(

&#x20;           set(clusters)

&#x20;       ):



&#x20;           cluster\_mask = (

&#x20;               clusters == cluster\_id

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           cluster\_embeddings = (

&#x20;               embeddings\[

&#x20;                   cluster\_mask

&#x20;               ]

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           centroid = (

&#x20;               cluster\_embeddings

&#x20;           if centroid\_norm > 0:



&#x20;               centroid = (

&#x20;                   centroid /

&#x20;                   centroid\_norm

&#x20;               )



&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;               cluster\_id

&#x20;           ] = centroid



&#x20;           cluster\_comments = \[

&#x20;               self.top20\_comments\[i]

&#x20;               for i in range(

&#x20;                   len(self.top20\_comments)

&#x20;               )

&#x20;               if clusters\[i] == cluster\_id

&#x20;           ]



&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_samples\[

&#x20;               cluster\_id

&#x20;           ] = cluster\_comments\[:3]



&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;       # IMPORTANT

&#x20;       #

&#x20;       # The top 20 comments are already embedded and assigned.

&#x20;       # Put them into the cache immediately.

&#x20;       # =====================================================



&#x20;       for comment, cluster\_id in zip(

&#x20;           self.top20\_comments,

&#x20;           clusters

&#x20;       ):



&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_cache\[

&#x20;               comment

&#x20;           ] = int(cluster\_id)



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;       )

\# =========================================================

&#x20;   # Step 5.6 Top Comment Clustering - APPLY

&#x20;   #

&#x20;   # PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZED VERSION

&#x20;   # =========================================================



&#x20;   def \_apply\_top20\_comment(self, df):



&#x20;       import re



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           "Feature Engineering - "

&#x20;           "Step 5.6 APPLY Comment Clustering"

&#x20;       )

&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;       # 1. CLEAN COMMENTS

&#x20;           df\["comment"]

&#x20;           .fillna("")

&#x20;           .astype(str)

&#x20;       def clean\_text(text):



&#x20;           text = re.sub(

&#x20;               r'ðÿ\\S\*',

&#x20;               ' ',

&#x20;               text

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           text = re.sub(

&#x20;               r'\[^a-z0-9\\s]',

&#x20;               ' ',

&#x20;               text

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           text = re.sub(

&#x20;               r'\\s+',

&#x20;               ' ',

&#x20;               text

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           return text.strip()



&#x20;       df\["comment\_clean"] = (

&#x20;           df\["comment"]

&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;       # 2. CHECK WHETHER MODEL EXISTS

&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;           df\["cluster"] = -1



&#x20;           df\["business\_categories"] = (

&#x20;               "Other / Acceptable Service"

&#x20;           )

&#x20;           return df



&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;       # 3. UNIQUE NON-EMPTY COMMENTS ONLY

&#x20;       # =====================================================



&#x20;       unique\_comments = (

&#x20;           df.loc\[

&#x20;           .tolist()

&#x20;           df\["cluster"] = -1

&#x20;           )



&#x20;           df\["sample\_comments"] = None



&#x20;           return df



&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;       # 4. CHECK CACHE

&#x20;       #

&#x20;       # Only comments that have NOT been seen before need

&#x20;       # SentenceTransformer embeddings.

&#x20;       # =====================================================



&#x20;       cached\_comments = \[]



&#x20;       new\_comments = \[]



&#x20;       for comment in unique\_comments:



&#x20;           if comment in self.comment\_cluster\_cache:



&#x20;               cached\_comments.append(

&#x20;                   comment

&#x20;               )



&#x20;           else:



&#x20;               new\_comments.append(

&#x20;                   comment

&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           f"Step 5.6 - Applying clustering to "

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;           f"Step 5.6 - Cached comments: "

&#x20;           f"{len(cached\_comments):,}"

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       print(

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;       # 5. BUILD CENTROID MATRIX

&#x20;       #

&#x20;       # This is built once for the current apply.

&#x20;       # =====================================================



&#x20;       cluster\_ids = list(

&#x20;           self.comment\_cluster\_centroids.keys()

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       centroid\_matrix = np.vstack(

&#x20;           \[

&#x20;               self.comment\_cluster\_centroids\[

&#x20;                   cluster\_id

&#x20;               ]

&#x20;               for cluster\_id in cluster\_ids

&#x20;           ]

&#x20;       )



&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;       # 6. EMBED ONLY NEW COMMENTS

&#x20;       #

&#x20;       # THIS IS THE MAIN PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT.

&#x20;       #

&#x20;       # Previously:

&#x20;       #

&#x20;       # 12,052 unique comments

&#x20;       # -> 12,052 SentenceTransformer embeddings

&#x20;       #

&#x20;       # Now:

&#x20;       # already cached -> 0 embeddings

&#x20;       # new comments   -> only new embeddings

&#x20;       # =====================================================



&#x20;       if new\_comments:



&#x20;           embeddings = (

&#x20;               self.comment\_embedding\_model.encode(

&#x20;                   new\_comments,

&#x20;           # =================================================

&#x20;           # 7. COSINE SIMILARITY

&#x20;           similarity\_matrix = (

&#x20;           best\_cluster\_indices = (

&#x20;               )

&#x20;           new\_cluster\_labels = \[

&#x20;           # =================================================

&#x20;           # 9. STORE NEW RESULTS IN CACHE

&#x20;           # =================================================



&#x20;           for comment, cluster\_id in zip(

&#x20;               new\_comments,

&#x20;               new\_cluster\_labels

&#x20;           ):



&#x20;               self.comment\_cluster\_cache\[

&#x20;                   comment

&#x20;               ] = int(cluster\_id)



&#x20;       # =====================================================

&#x20;       # 10. COMMENT -> CLUSTER LOOKUP
